1.1: The Visions of Isaiah son of Amoz, that he has seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
1.2: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, For Jehovah has spoken: Sons I have nourished and brought up, And they--they transgressed against Me.
1.3: An ox has known its owner, And an ass the crib of its master, Israel has not known, My people has not understood.
1.4: Ah, sinning nation, a people heavy with iniquity, A seed of evil doers, sons--corrupters! They have forsaken Jehovah, They have despised the Holy One of Israel, They have gone away backward.
1.5: Wherefore are you stricken any more? You do add apostasy! Every head is become diseased, and every heart is sick.
1.6: From the sole of the foot--to the head, There is no soundness in it, Wound, and bruise, and fresh smiting! They have not been closed nor bound, Nor have they softened with ointment.
1.7: Your land is a desolation, your cities burnt with fire, Your ground, before you strangers are consuming it, And a desolation as overthrown by strangers!
1.8: And left has been the daughter of Zion, As a booth in a vineyard, As a lodge in a place of cucumbers--as a city besieged.
1.9: Unless Jehovah of Hosts had left to us a remnant, Shortly--as Sodom we had been, To Gomorrah we had been like!
1.10: Hear the word of Jehovah, you rulers of Sodom, Give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah,
1.11: `Why to Me the abundance of your sacrifices? says Jehovah, I have been satiated with burnt-offerings of rams, And fat of fatlings; And blood of bullocks, and lambs, And he-goats I have not desired.
1.12: When you come in to appear before Me, Who has required this of your hand, To trample My courts?
1.13: Add not to bring in a vain present, Incense--an abomination it is to Me, New moon, and sabbath, calling of convocation! Rendure not iniquity--and a restraint!
1.14: Your new moons and your set seasons has My soul hated, They have been upon me for a burden, I have been weary of bearing.
1.15: And in your spreading forth your hands, I hide my eyes from you, Also when you increase prayer, I do not hear, Your hands of blood have been full.
1.16: Wash you, make you pure, Turn aside the evil of your doings, from before My eyes, Cease to do evil, learn to do good.
1.17: Seek judgment, make happy the oppressed, Judge the fatherless, strive for the widow.
1.18: Come, I pray you, and we reason, says Jehovah, If your sins are as scarlet, as snow they shall be white, If they are red as crimson, as wool they shall be!
1.19: If you are willing, and have hearkened, The good of the land you consume,
1.20: And if you refuse, and have rebelled, By the sword you are consumed, For the mouth of Jehovah has spoken.
1.21: How has a faithful city become a harlot? I have filled it with judgment, Righteousness lodges in it--now murderers.
1.22: Your silver has become dross, Your drink polluted with water.
1.23: Your princes are apostates, and companions of thieves, Every one loving a bribe, and pursuing rewards, The fatherless they judge not, And the plea of the widow comes not to them.
1.24: Therefore--the affirmation of the Lord--Jehovah of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah, I am eased of My adversaries, And I am avenged of My enemies,
1.25: And I turn back My hand upon you, And I refine as purity your dross, And I turn aside all your tin,
1.26: And I give back your judges as at the first, And your counsellors as in the beginning, After this you are called, `A city of righteousness--a faithful city.'
1.27: Zion in judgment is redeemed, And her captivity in righteousness.
1.28: And the destruction of transgressors and sinners is together, And those forsaking Jehovah are consumed.
1.29: For men are ashamed because of the oaks That you have desired, And you are confounded because of the gardens That you have chosen.
1.30: For you are as an oak whose leaf is fading, And as a garden that has no water.
1.31: And the strong has been for tow, And his work for a spark, And burned have both of them together, And there is none quenching!

2.1: The thing that Isaiah son of Amoz has seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
2.2: And it has come to pass, In the latter end of the days, Established is the mount of Jehovah's house, Above the top of the mounts, And it has been lifted up above the heights, And flowed to it have all the nations.
2.3: And gone have many peoples and said, `Come, and we go up to the mount of Jehovah, To the house of the God of Jacob, And He does teach us of His ways, And we walk in His paths, For from Zion goes forth a law, And a word of Jehovah from Jerusalem.
2.4: And He has judged between the nations, And has given a decision to many peoples, And they have beat their swords to ploughshares, And their spears to pruning-hooks, Nation does not lift up sword to nation, Nor do they learn any more--war.
2.5: O house of Jacob, come, And we walk in the light of Jehovah.'
2.6: For You have left Your people, the house of Jacob. For they have been filled from the east, And are sorcerers like the Philistines, And with the children of strangers strike hands.
2.7: And its land is full of silver and gold, And there is no end to its treasures, And its land is full of horses, And there is no end to its chariots,
2.8: And its land is full of idols, To the work of its hands it bows itself, To that which its fingers have made,
2.9: And the low bows down, and the high is humbled, And You accept them not.
2.10: Enter into a rock, and be hidden in dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency.
2.11: The haughty eyes of man have been humbled, And bowed down has been the loftiness of men, And set on high has Jehovah alone been in that day.
2.12: For a day is to Jehovah of Hosts, For every proud and high one, And for every lifted up and low one,
2.13: And for all cedars of Lebanon, The high and the exalted ones, And for all oaks of Bashan,
2.14: And for all the high mountains, And for all the exalted heights,
2.15: And for every high tower, And for every fenced wall,
2.16: And for all ships of Tarshish, And for all desirable pictures.
2.17: And bowed down has been the haughtiness of man, And humbled the loftiness of men, And set on high has Jehovah alone been in that day.
2.18: And the idols--they completely pass away.
2.19: And men have entered into caverns of rocks, And into caves of dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
2.20: In that day does man cast his idols of silver, And his idols of gold, That they have made for him to worship, To moles, and to bats,
2.21: To enter into cavities of the rocks, And into clefts of the high places, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
2.22: Cease for you from man, Whose breath is in his nostrils, For--in what is he esteemed?

3.1: For, indeed, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is turning aside from Jerusalem, And from Judah, stay and staff, Every stay of bread, and every stay of water.
3.2: Hero and man of war, judge and prophet, And diviner and elder,
3.3: Head of fifty, and accepted of faces, And counsellor, and the wise of artificers, And the intelligent of charmers.
3.4: And I have made youths their heads, And sucklings rule over them.
3.5: And the people has exacted--man upon man, Even a man on his neighbour, Enlarge themselves do the youths against the aged, And the lightly esteemed against the honoured.
3.6: When one lays hold on his brother, Of the house of his father, by the garment, `Come, a ruler you are to us, And this ruin is under your hand.'
3.7: He lifts up, in that day, saying: `I am not a binder up, And in my house is neither bread nor garment, You do not make me a ruler of the people.'
3.8: For stumbled has Jerusalem, and Judah has fallen, For their tongue and their doings are against Jehovah, To provoke the eyes of His glory.
3.9: The appearance of their faces witnessed against them, And their sin, as Sodom, they declared, They have not hidden! Woe to their soul, For they have done to themselves evil.
3.10: Say you to the righteous, that it is good, Because the fruit of their doings they eat.
3.11: Woe to the wicked--evil, Because the deed of his hand is done to him.
3.12: My people--its exactors are sucklings, And women have ruled over it. My people--your eulogists are causing to err, And the way of your paths swallowed up.
3.13: Jehovah has stood up to plead, And He is standing to judge the peoples.
3.14: Jehovah into judgment does enter With elders of His people, and its heads: `And you, you have consumed the vineyard, Plunder of the poor is in your houses.
3.15: What--to you? you bruise My people, And the faces of the poor you grind.' An affirmation of the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, And Jehovah says:
3.16: `Because that daughters of Zion have been haughty, And they walk stretching out the neck, And deceiving with the eyes, Walking and mincing they go, And with their feet they make a tinkling,
3.17: The Lord also has scabbed The crown of the head of daughters of Zion, And Jehovah their simplicity exposes.
3.18: In that day does the Lord turn aside The beauty of the tinkling ornaments, And of the embroidered works, And of the round tires like moons,
3.19: Of the drops, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,
3.20: Of the bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, And of the bands, And of the perfume boxes, and the amulets,
3.21: Of the seals, and of the nose-rings,
3.22: Of the costly apparel, and of the mantles, And of the coverings, and of the purses,
3.23: Of the mirrors, and of the linen garments, And of the hoods, and of the vails,
3.24: And it has been, instead of spice is muck, And instead of a girdle, a rope, And instead of curled work, baldness, And instead of a stomacher a girdle of sackcloth.
3.25: For instead of glory, your men by sword do fall, And your might in battle.
3.26: And lamented and mourned have her openings, Yes, she has been emptied, on the earth she sits!

4.1: And taken hold have seven women on one man, In that day, saying, `Our own bread we do eat, And our own raiment we put on, Only, let your name be called over us, Remove you our reproach.'
4.2: In that day is the Shoot of Jehovah for desire and for honour, And the fruit of the earth For excellence and for beauty to the escaped of Israel.
4.3: And it has been, he who is left in Zion, And he who is remaining in Jerusalem, `Holy' is said of him, Of every one who is written for life in Jerusalem.
4.4: If the Lord has washed away The filth of daughters of Zion, And the blood of Jerusalem purges from her midst, By the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
4.5: Then has Jehovah prepared Over every fixed place of Mount Zion, And over her convocations, A cloud by day, and smoke, And the shining of a flaming fire by night, That, over all honour a safe-guard,
4.6: And a covering may be, For a shadow by day from drought, And for a refuge, and for a hiding place, From inundation and from rain!

5.1: Let me sing, I pray you, for my beloved, A song of my beloved as to his vineyard: My beloved has a vineyard in a fruitful hill,
5.2: And he fences it, and casts out its stones, And plants it with a choice vine, And builds a tower in its midst, And also a wine press has hewn out in it, And he waits for the yielding of grapes, And it yields bad ones!
5.3: And now, O inhabitant of Jerusalem, and man of Judah, Judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard.
5.4: What--to do still to my vineyard, That I have not done in it! Wherefore, I waited to the yielding of grapes, And it yields bad ones!
5.5: And now, pray, let me cause you to know, That which I am doing to my vineyard, To turn aside its hedge, And it has been for consumption, To break down its wall, And it has been for a treading-place.
5.6: And I make it a waste, It is not pruned, nor arranged, And gone up have brier and thorn, And on the thick clouds I lay a charge, From raining upon it rain.
5.7: Because the vineyard of Jehovah of Hosts Is the house of Israel, And the man of Judah His pleasant plant, And He waits for judgment, and indeed, oppression, For righteousness, and indeed, a cry.
5.8: Woe to those joining house to house, Field to field they bring near, till there is no place, And you have been settled by yourselves In the midst of the land!
5.9: By the weapons of Jehovah of Hosts Do not many houses a desolation become? Great and good without inhabitant!
5.10: For ten acres of vineyard do yield one bath, And an homer of seed yields an ephah.
5.11: Woe to those rising early in the morning, Strong drink they pursue! Tarrying in twilight, wine inflames them!
5.12: And harp, and psaltery, tabret, and pipe, And wine, have been their banquets, And the work of Jehovah they behold not, Yes, the work of His hands they have not seen.
5.13: Therefore my people removed without knowledge, And its honourable ones are famished, And its multitude dried up of thirst.
5.14: Therefore has Sheol enlarged herself, And has opened her mouth without limit. And gone down has its honour, and its multitude, And its noise, and its exulting one--into her.
5.15: And bowed down is the low, and humbled the high, And the eyes of the haughty become low,
5.16: And Jehovah of Hosts is high in judgment, And the Holy God sanctified in righteousness,
5.17: And fed have lambs according to their leading, And waste places of the fat ones Do sojourners consume.
5.18: Woe to those drawing out iniquity with cords of vanity, And as with thick ropes of the cart--sin.
5.19: Who are saying, `Let Him hurry, Let Him hasten His work, that we may see, And let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel Draw near and come, and we know.'
5.20: Woe to those saying to evil `good,' And to good `evil,' Putting darkness for light, and light for darkness, Putting bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter.
5.21: Woe to the wise in their own eyes, And--before their own faces--intelligent!
5.22: Woe to the mighty to drink wine, And men of strength to mingle strong drink.
5.23: Declaring righteous the wicked for a bribe, And the righteousness of the righteous They turn aside from him.
5.24: Therefore, as a tongue of fire devours stubble, And flaming hay falls, Their root is as muck, And their flower as dust goes up. Because they have rejected the law of Jehovah of Hosts, And the saying of the Holy One of Israel despised.
5.25: Therefore has the anger of Jehovah burned among His people, And He stretches out His hand against it, And smites it, and the mountains tremble, And their carcase is as filth in the midst of the out-places. With all this His anger did not turn back, And still His hand is stretched out!
5.26: And He lifted up an ensign to nations afar off, And hissed to it from the end of the earth, And indeed, with haste, swift it comes.
5.27: There is none weary, nor stumbling in it, It does not slumber, nor sleep, Nor opened has been the girdle of its loins, Nor drawn away the latchet of its sandals.
5.28: Whose arrows are sharp, and all its bows bent, Hoofs of its horses as flint have been reckoned, And its wheels as a hurricane!
5.29: Its roaring is like a lioness, It roars like young lions, And it howls, and seizes prey, And carries away safely, and there is none delivering.
5.30: And it howls against it in that day as the howling of a sea, And it has looked attentively to the land, And indeed, darkness--distress, And light has been darkened by its abundance!

6.1: In the year of the death of king Uzziah--I see the Lord, sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and His train is filling the temple.
6.2: Seraphs are standing above it: six wings has each one; with two each covers its face, and with two each covers its feet, and with two each flies.
6.3: And this one has called to that, and has said: `Holy, Holy, Holy, is Jehovah of Hosts, The fulness of all the earth is His glory.'
6.4: And the posts of the thresholds are moved by the voice of him who is calling, and the house is full of smoke.
6.5: And I say, `Woe to me, for I have been silent, For a man--unclean of lips am I, And in midst of a people unclean of lips I am dwelling, Because the King, Jehovah of Hosts, have my eyes seen.'
6.6: And flee to me does one of the seraphs, and in his hand a burning coal, (with tongs he has taken it from off the altar,)
6.7: and he strikes against my mouth, and says: `Indeed, this has stricken against your lips, And turned aside is yours iniquity, And your sin is covered.'
6.8: And I hear the voice of the Lord, saying: `Whom do I send? and who does go for Us?' And I say, `Here am I, send me.'
6.9: And He says, `Go, and you have said to this people, Hear you--to hear, and you do not understand, And see you--to see, and you do not know.
6.10: Declare fat the heart of this people, And its ears declare heavy, And its eyes declare dazzled, Lest it see with its eyes, And with its ears hear, and its heart consider, And it has turned back, and has health.'
6.11: And I say, `Till when, O Lord?' And He says, `Surely till cities have been wasted without inhabitant, And houses without man, And the ground be wasted--a desolation,
6.12: And Jehovah has put man far off, And great is the forsaken part in the heart of the land.
6.13: And yet in it a tenth, and it has turned, And has been for a burning, As a teil-tree, and as an oak, that in falling, Have substance in them, The holy seed is its substance!'

7.1: And it comes to pass in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, gone up has Rezin king of Aram, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, to Jerusalem, to battle against it, and he is not able to fight against it.
7.2: And it is declared to the house of David, saying, `Aram has been led toward Ephraim,' And his heart and the heart of his people is moved, like the moving of trees of a forest by the presence of wind.
7.3: And Jehovah says to Isaiah, `Go forth, I pray you, to meet Ahaz, you, and Shear-Jashub your son, to the end of the conduit of the upper pool, to the highway of the fuller's field,
7.4: and you have said to him: `Take heed, and be quiet, fear not, And let not your heart be timid, Because of these two tails of smoking brands, For the fierceness of the anger of Rezin and Aram, And the son of Remaliah.
7.5: Because that Aram counselled against you evil, Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:
7.6: We go up into Judah, and we vex it, And we rend it to ourselves, And we cause a king to reign in its midst--The son of Tabeal.
7.7: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: It does not stand, nor shall it be!
7.8: For the head of Aram is Damascus, And the head of Damascus is Rezin, And within sixty and five years Is Ephraim broken from being a people.
7.9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, And the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not give credence, Surely you are not stedfast.'
7.10: And Jehovah adds to speak to Ahaz, saying:
7.11: `Ask for you a sign from Jehovah your God, Make deep the request, or make it high upwards.'
7.12: And Ahaz says, `I do not ask nor try Jehovah.'
7.13: And he says, `Hear, I pray you, O house of David, Is it a little thing for you to weary men, That you weary also my God?
7.14: Therefore the Lord Himself gives to you a sign, Indeed, the Virgin is conceiving, And is bringing forth a son, And has called his name Immanuel,
7.15: Butter and honey he does eat, When he knows to refuse evil, and to fix on good.
7.16: For before the youth does know To refuse evil, and to fix on good, Forsaken is the land you are vexed with, because of her two kings.
7.17: Jehovah brings on you, and on your people, And on the house of your father, Days that have not come, Even from the day of the turning aside of Ephraim from Judah, By the king of Asshur.
7.18: And it has come to pass, in that day, Jehovah does hiss for a fly that is in the extremity of the brooks of Egypt, And for a bee that is in the land of Asshur.
7.19: And they have come, and rested all of them in the desolate valleys, And in holes of the rocks, and on all the thorns, And on all the commendable things.
7.20: In that day does the Lord shave, By a razor that is hired beyond the river, By the king of Asshur, The head, and the hair of the feet, Yes, also the beard it consumes.
7.21: And it has come to pass, in that day, A man keeps alive a heifer of the herd, And two of the flock,
7.22: And it has come to pass, From the abundance of the yielding of milk he eats butter, For butter and honey does every one eat Who is left in the heart of the land.
7.23: And it has come to pass, in that day, Every place where there are a thousand vines, At a thousand silverlings, Is for briers and for thorns.
7.24: With arrows and with bow he comes there, Because all the land is brier and thorn.
7.25: And all the hills that with a mattock are kept in order, There comes not the fear of brier and thorn, And it has been for the sending forth of ox, And for the treading of sheep!'

8.1: And Jehovah says to me, `Take to you a great tablet, and write upon it with a graving tool of man, To haste spoil, enjoy prey.'
8.2: And I cause faithful witnesses to testify to me, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
8.3: And I draw near to the prophetess, and she conceives, and bears a son; and Jehovah says to me, `Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz,
8.4: for before the youth does know to cry, My father, and My mother, one takes away the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria, before the king of Asshur.'
8.5: And Jehovah adds to speak to me again, saying:
8.6: `Because that this people has refused The waters of Shiloah that go softly, And is rejoicing with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
8.7: Therefore, indeed, the Lord is bringing up on them, The waters of the river, the mighty and the great, (The king of Asshur, and all his glory,) And it has gone up over all its streams, And has gone on over all its banks.
8.8: And it has passed on into Judah, It has overflown and passed over, To the neck it comes, And the stretching out of its wings Has been the fulness of the breadth of your land, O Emmanu-El!
8.9: Be friends, O nations, and be broken, And give ear, all you far off ones of earth, Gird yourselves, and be broken, Gird yourselves, and be broken.
8.10: Take counsel, and it is broken, Speak a word, and it does not stand, Because of Emmanu-El!'
8.11: For thus has Jehovah spoken to me with strength of hand, and instructs me against walking in the way of this people, saying,
8.12: `You do not say, A confederacy, To all to whom this people says, A confederacy, And its fear you do not fear, Nor declare fearful.
8.13: Jehovah of Hosts--Him you do sanctify, And He is your Fear, and He your Dread,
8.14: And He has been for a sanctuary, And for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of falling, To the two houses of Israel, For a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
8.15: And many among them have stumbled and fallen, And been broken, and snared, and captured.
8.16: Bind up the testimony, Seal the law among My disciples.
8.17: And I have waited for Jehovah, Who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob, And I have looked for Him.
8.18: Indeed, I, and the children whom Jehovah has given to me, Are for signs and for wonders in Israel, From Jehovah of Hosts, who is dwelling in Mount Zion.
8.19: And when they say to you, `Seek to those having familiar spirits, And to wizards, who chatter and mutter, Does not a people seek to its God? --For the living to the dead!
8.20: To the law and to the testimony! If not, let them say after this manner, `That there is no dawn to it.'
8.21: --And it has passed over into it, hardened and hungry, And it has come to pass, That it is hungry, and has been wroth, And made light of its king, and of its God, And has looked upwards.
8.22: And to the land it looks attentively, And indeed, adversity and darkness! --Dimness, distress, and thick darkness is driven away, But not the dimness for which she is in distress!

9.1: As the former time made light The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, So the latter has honoured the way of the sea, Beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
9.2: The people who are walking in darkness Have seen a great light, Dwellers in a land of death-shade, Light has shone upon them.
9.3: You have multiplied the nation, You have made great its joy, They have joyed before You as the joy in harvest, As men rejoice in their apportioning spoil.
9.4: Because the yoke of its burden, And the staff of its shoulder, the rod of its exactor, You have broken as in the day of Midian.
9.5: For every battle of a warrior is with rushing, and raiment rolled in blood, And it has been for burning--fuel of fire.
9.6: For a Child has been born to us, A Son has been given to us, And the princely power is on his shoulder, And He does call his name Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.
9.7: To the increase of the princely power, And of peace, there is no end, On the throne of David, and on his kingdom, To establish it, and to support it, In judgment and in righteousness, Now, even to the age, The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts does this.
9.8: A word has the Lord sent into Jacob, And it has fallen in Israel.
9.9: And the people have known--all of it, Ephraim, and the inhabitant of Samaria, In pride and in greatness of heart, saying,
9.10: `Bricks have fallen, and hewn work we build, Sycamores have been cut down, and cedars we renew.'
9.11: And Jehovah sets the adversaries of Rezin on high above him, And his enemies he joins together,
9.12: Aram from before, and Philistia from behind, And they devour Israel with the whole mouth. With all this not turned back has His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
9.13: And the people has not turned back to Him who is smiting it, And Jehovah of Hosts they have not sought.
9.14: And Jehovah cuts off from Israel head and tail, Branch and reed--the same day,
9.15: Elder, and accepted of face, he is the head, Prophet, teacher of falsehood, he is the tail.
9.16: And the eulogists of this people are causing to err, And its eulogised ones are consumed.
9.17: Therefore, over its young men the Lord rejoices not, And its orphans, and its widows He pities not, For every one is profane, and an evil doer, And every mouth is speaking folly. With all this not turned back has His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
9.18: For burned as a fire has wickedness, Brier and thorn it devours, And it kindles in thickets of the forest, And they lift themselves up, an exaltation of smoke!
9.19: In the wrath of Jehovah of Hosts Has the land been consumed, And the people is as fuel of fire; A man on his brother has no pity,
9.20: And cuts down on the right, and has been hungry, And he devours on the left, And they have not been satisfied, Each the flesh of his own arm they devour.
9.21: Manasseh--Ephraim, and Ephraim--Manasseh, Together they are against Judah, With all this not turned back has His anger. And still His hand is stretched out!

10.1: Woe to those decreeing decrees of iniquity, And writers who have prescribed perverseness.
10.2: To turn aside from judgment the poor, And to take violently away the judgment Of the afflicted of My people, That widows may be their prey, That the fatherless they may spoil.
10.3: And what do you at a day of inspection? And at desolation? --from afar it comes. Near whom do you flee for help? And where do you leave your honour?
10.4: Without Me it has bowed down In the place of a bound one, And in the place of the slain they fall. With all this not turned back has His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
10.5: Woe to Asshur, a rod of My anger, And a staff in their hand is My indignation.
10.6: Against a profane nation I send him, And concerning a people of My wrath I charge him, To spoil spoil, and to seize prey, And to make it a treading-place as the clay of out places.
10.7: And he--he thinks not so, And his heart reckons not so, For--to destroy is in his heart, And to cut off nations not a few.
10.8: For he says, `Are not my princes altogether kings?
10.9: Is not Calno as Carchemish? Is not Hamath as Arpad? Is not Samaria as Damascus?
10.10: As my hand has got to the kingdoms of a worthless thing, and their graven images, Greater than Jerusalem and than Samaria,
10.11: Do I not--as I have done to Samaria, And to her worthless things, So do to Jerusalem and to her grievous things?
10.12: And it has come to pass, When the Lord does fulfil all His work In mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I see concerning the fruit of the greatness Of the heart of the king of Asshur. And concerning the glory of the height of his eyes.
10.13: For he has said, `By the power of my hand I have worked, And by my wisdom, for I have been intelligent, And I remove borders of the peoples, And their chief ones I have spoiled, And I put down as a mighty one the inhabitants,
10.14: And my hand as to a nest Gets to the wealth of the peoples, And as a gathering of forsaken eggs All the earth I--I have gathered, And there has not been one moving wing, Or opening mouth, or whispering.'
10.15: --Does the axe glorify itself Against him who is hewing with it? Does the saw magnify itself Against him who is shaking it? As a rod waving those lifting it up! As a staff lifting up that which is not wood!
10.16: Therefore does the Lord, the Lord of Hosts, Send among his fat ones leanness, And under his honour He kindles a burning As the burning of a fire.
10.17: And the light of Israel has been for a fire, And his Holy One for a flame, And it has burned, and devoured his thorn And his brier in one day.
10.18: And the honour of his forest, and his fruitful field, From soul even to flesh He does consume, And it has been as the fainting of a standard-bearer.
10.19: And the rest of the trees of his forest are few, And a youth does write them.
10.20: And it has come to pass, in that day, The remnant of Israel, And the escaped of the house of Jacob, Do not add any more to lean on its smiter, And have leant on Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, in truth.
10.21: A remnant returns--a remnant of Jacob, To the Mighty God.
10.22: For though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, A remnant does return of it, A consumption determined, Overflowing with righteousness.
10.23: For a consumption that is determined, The Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is making in the midst of all the land.
10.24: Therefore, thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, `Be not afraid, my people, inhabiting Zion, because of Asshur, With a rod he does smite you, And his staff lifts up against you, in the way of Egypt.
10.25: For yet a very little, And the indignation has been completed, And My anger by their wearing out.
10.26: And awaking for him is Jehovah of Hosts, A scourge like the smiting of Midian at the rock Oreb, And his rod is over the sea, And he has lifted it in the way of Egypt.
10.27: And it has come to pass, in that day, Turned is his burden from off your shoulder, And his yoke from off your neck, And destroyed has been the yoke, because of prosperity.
10.28: He has come in against Aiath, He has passed over into Migron, At Michmash he looks after his vessels.
10.29: They have gone over the passage, Geba they have made a lodging place, Trembled has Rama, Gibeah of Saul fled.
10.30: Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim, Give attention, Laish! answer her, Anathoth.
10.31: Fled away has Madmenah, The inhabitants of the high places have hardened themselves.
10.32: Yet to-day in Nob to remain, Wave its hand does the mount of the daughter of Zion, The hill of Jerusalem.
10.33: Indeed, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is lopping a branch with violence, And the high of stature are cut down, And the lofty are become low,
10.34: And He has gone round the thickets of the forest with iron, And Lebanon by a mighty one falls!

11.1: And a rod has come out from the stock of Jesse, And a branch from his roots is fruitful.
11.2: Rested on him has the Spirit of Jehovah, The spirit of wisdom and understanding, The spirit of counsel and might, The spirit of knowledge and fear of Jehovah.
11.3: To refresh him in the fear of Jehovah, And by the sight of his eyes he judges not, Nor by the hearing of his ears decides.
11.4: And he has judged in righteousness the poor, And decided in uprightness for the humble of earth, And has smitten earth with the rod of his mouth, And with the breath of his lips he puts the wicked to death.
11.5: And righteousness has been the girdle of his loins, And faithfulness--the girdle of his reins.
11.6: And a wolf has sojourned with a lamb, And a leopard with a kid does lie down, And calf, and young lion, and fatling are together, And a little youth is leader over them.
11.7: And cow and bear do feed, Together lie down their young ones, And a lion as an ox eats straw.
11.8: And played has a suckling by the hole of an asp, And on the den of a cockatrice Has the weaned one put his hand.
11.9: Evil they do not, nor destroy in all My holy mountain, For full has been the earth with the knowledge of Jehovah, As the waters are covering the sea.
11.10: And there has been, in that day, A root of Jesse that is standing for an ensign of peoples, To him do nations seek, And his rest has been--honour!
11.11: And it has come to pass, in that day, The Lord adds a second time his power, To get the remnant of His people that is left, From Asshur, and from Egypt, And from Pathros, and from Cush, And from Elam, and from Shinar, And from Hamath, and from isles of the sea,
11.12: And He has lifted up an ensign to nations, And gathers the driven away of Israel, And the scattered of Judah He assembles, From the four wings of the earth.
11.13: And turned aside has the envy of Ephraim, And the adversaries of Judah are cut off, Ephraim does not envy Judah, And Judah does not distress Ephraim.
11.14: And they have flown on the shoulder of the Philistines westward, Together they spoil the sons of the east, Edom and Moab sending forth their hand, And sons of Ammon obeying them.
11.15: And Jehovah has devoted to destruction The tongue of the sea of Egypt, And has waved His hand over the river, In the terror of his wind, And has smitten it at the seven streams, And has caused men to tread it with shoes.
11.16: And there has been a highway, For the remnant of His people that is left, from Asshur, As there was for Israel in the day of his coming up out of the land of Egypt!

12.1: And you have said in that day: `I thank you, O Jehovah, Though You have been angry with me, Turn back does Your anger, And You do comfort me.
12.2: Indeed, God is my salvation, I trust, and fear not, For my strength and song is Jah Jehovah, And He is to me for salvation.
12.3: And you have drawn waters with joy Out of the fountains of salvation,
12.4: And you have said in that day, Give you praise to Jehovah, call in His name. Make known among the peoples His acts. Make mention that set on high is His name.
12.5: Praise you Jehovah, for excellence He has done, Known is this in all the earth.
12.6: Cry aloud, and sing, O inhabitant of Zion, For great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel!'

13.1: The burden of Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz has seen:
13.2: `On a high mountain lift you up an ensign, Raise the voice to them, wave the hand, And they go in to the openings of nobles.
13.3: I have given charge to My sanctified ones, Also I have called My mighty ones for My anger, Those rejoicing at My excellency.'
13.4: A voice of a multitude in the mountains, A likeness of a numerous people, A voice of noise from the kingdoms of nations who are gathered, Jehovah of Hosts inspecting a host of battle!
13.5: They are coming in from a land afar off, From the end of the heavens, Jehovah and the instruments of His indignation, To destroy all the land.
13.6: Howl you, for near is the day of Jehovah, As destruction from the Mighty it comes.
13.7: Therefore, all hands do fail, And every heart of man does melt.
13.8: And they have been troubled, Pains and pangs they take, As a travailing woman they are pained, A man at his friend they marvel, The appearance of flames--their faces!
13.9: Indeed, the day of Jehovah does come, Fierce, with wrath, and heat of anger, To make the land become a desolation, Yes, its sinning ones He destroys from it.
13.10: For the stars of the heavens, and their constellations, Cause not their light to shine, Darkened has been the sun in its going out, And the moon causes not its light to come forth.
13.11: And I have appointed on the world evil, And on the wicked their iniquity, And have caused to cease the excellency of the proud, And the excellency of the terrible I make low.
13.12: I make man more rare than fine gold, And a common man than pure gold of Ophir.
13.13: Therefore the heavens I cause to tremble, And the earth does shake from its place, In the wrath of Jehovah of Hosts, And in a day of the heat of his anger.
13.14: And it has been, as a roe driven away, And as a flock that has no gatherer, Each to his people--they turn, And each to his land--they flee.
13.15: Every one who is found is thrust through, And every one who is added falls by sword.
13.16: And their sucklings are dashed to pieces before their eyes, Spoiled are their houses, and their wives lain with.
13.17: Indeed, I am stirring up against them the Medes, Who silver esteem not, And gold--they delight not in it.
13.18: And bows dash young men to pieces, And the fruit of the womb they pity not, On sons their eye has no pity.
13.19: And Babylon, the beauty of kingdoms, The glory, the excellency of the Chaldeans, Has been as overthrown by God, With Sodom and with Gomorrah.
13.20: She does not sit for ever, Nor continues to many generations, Nor does Arab pitch tent there, And shepherds lie not down there.
13.21: And Ziim have lain down there, And full have been their houses of howlings, And dwelt there have daughters of an ostrich, And goats do skip there.
13.22: And Aiim have responded in his forsaken habitations, And dragons in palaces of delight, And near to come is her time, And her days are not drawn out!

14.1: Because Jehovah loves Jacob, And has fixed again on Israel, And given them rest on their own land, And joined has been the sojourner to them, And they have been admitted to the house of Jacob.
14.2: And peoples have taken them, And have brought them in to their place, And the house of Israel have inherited them, On the land of Jehovah, For men-servants and for maid-servants, And they have been captors of their captors, And have ruled over their exactors.
14.3: And it has come to pass, In the day of Jehovah's giving rest to you, From your grief, and from your trouble, And from the sharp bondage, That has been served upon you,
14.4: That you have taken up this simile Concerning the king of Babylon, and said, How has the exactor ceased,
14.5: Ceased has the golden one. Broken has Jehovah the staff of the wicked, The sceptre of rulers.
14.6: He who is smiting peoples in wrath, A smiting without intermission, He who is ruling in anger nations, Pursuing without restraint!
14.7: At rest--quiet has been all the earth, They have broken forth into singing.
14.8: Even firs have rejoiced over you, Cedars of Lebanon-- saying: Since you have lain down, The hewer comes not up against us.
14.9: Sheol beneath has been troubled at you, To meet your coming in, It is waking up for you Rephaim, All chiefs ones of earth, It has raised up from their thrones All kings of nations.
14.10: All of them answer and say to you, Even you have become weak like us! To us you have become like!
14.11: Brought down to Sheol has been yours excellency, The noise of your psaltery, Under you spread out has been the worm, Yes, covering you is the worm.
14.12: How have you fallen from the heavens, O shining one, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to earth, O weakener of nations.
14.13: And you said in your heart: the heavens I go up, Above stars of God I raise my throne, And I sit in the mount of meeting in the sides of the north.
14.14: I go up above the heights of a thick cloud, I am like to the Most High.
14.15: Only--to Sheol you are brought down, To the sides of the pit.
14.16: Your beholders look to you, to you they attend, Is this the man causing the earth to tremble, Shaking kingdoms?
14.17: He has made the world as a wilderness, And his cities he has broken down, Of his bound ones he opened not the house.
14.18: All kings of nations--all of them, Have lain down in honour, each in his house,
14.19: And--you have been cast out of your grave, As an abominable branch, raiment of the slain, Thrust through ones of the sword, Going down to the sons of the pit, As a carcase trodden down.
14.20: You are not united with them in burial, For your land you have destroyed, Your people you have slain, Not named to the age is the seed of evil doers.
14.21: Prepare you for his sons slaughter; Because of the iniquity of their fathers, They rise not, nor have possessed the land, Nor filled the face of the world with cities.
14.22: And I have risen up against them, (The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts,) And have cut off, in reference to Babylon, Name and remnant, and continuator and successor, The affirmation of Jehovah.
14.23: And have made it for a possession of a bittern, And ponds of waters, And daubed it with the mire of destruction, The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts!
14.24: Sworn has Jehovah of Hosts, saying, `As I thought--so has it not been? And as I counselled--it stands;
14.25: To break Asshur in My land, And on My mountains I tread him down, And turned from off them has his yoke, Yes, his burden from off their shoulder turns aside.
14.26: This is the counsel that is counselled for all the earth, And this is the hand that is stretched out for all the nations.
14.27: For Jehovah of Hosts has purposed, And who does make void? And His hand that is stretched out, Who does turn it back?'
14.28: In the year of the death of king Ahaz was this burden:
14.29: Rejoice not you, Philistia, all of you, That broken has been the rod of your smiter, For from the root of a serpent comes out a viper, And its fruit is a flying saraph.
14.30: And delighted have the first-born of the poor, And the needy in confidence lie down, And I have put to death with famine your root, And your remnant it slays.
14.31: Howl, O gate; cry, O city, Melted are you, Philistia, all of you, For from the north smoke has come, And there is none alone in his set places.
14.32: And what does one answer the messengers of a nation? `That Jehovah has founded Zion, And in it do the poor of His people trust!'

15.1: The burden of Moab. Because in a night destroyed was Ar of Moab--It has been cut off, Because in a night destroyed was Kir of Moab--It has been cut off.
15.2: He has gone up to Bajith and Dibon, The high places--to weep, On Nebo and on Medeba Moab howls, On all its heads is baldness, every beard cut off.
15.3: In its out-places they girded on sackcloth, On its pinnacles, and in its broad places, Every one howls--going down with weeping.
15.4: And cry does Heshbon and Elealeh, To Jahaz heard has been their voice, Therefore the armed ones of Moab do shout, His life has been grievous to him.
15.5: My heart is toward Moab, Cry do her fugitives to Zoar, a heifer of the third year, For--the ascent of Luhith--With weeping he goes up in it, For, in the way of Horonaim, A cry of destruction they wake up.
15.6: For, the waters of Nimrim are desolations, For, withered has been the hay, Finished has been the tender grass, A green thing there has not been.
15.7: Therefore the abundance he made, and their store, To the brook of the willows they carry.
15.8: For gone round has the cry the border of Moab, To Eglaim is its howling, And to Beer-Elim is its howling.
15.9: For the waters of Dimon have been full of blood, For I set on Dimon additions, For the escaped of Moab a lion, And for the remnant of Adamah!

16.1: Send you a lamb to the ruler of the land, From Selah in the wilderness, To the mount of the daughter of Zion.
16.2: And it has come to pass, As a wandering bird, a nest cast out, Are daughters of Moab, at fords of Arnon.
16.3: Bring you in counsel, do judgment, Make as night your shadow in the midst of noon, Hide outcasts, the wanderer reveal not.
16.4: Sojourn in you do My outcasts, O Moab, Be a secret hiding-place to them, From the face of a destroyer, For ceased has the extortioner, Finished has been a destroyer, Consumed the treaders down out of the land.
16.5: And established in kindness is the throne, And one has sat on it in truth, in the tent of David, Judging and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.
16.6: We have heard of the pride of Moab--very proud, His pride, and his arrogance, and his wrath, Not right are his devices.
16.7: Therefore howl does Moab for Moab, all of it does howl, For the grape-cakes of Kir-Hareseth it meditates, Surely they are smitten.
16.8: Because fields of Heshbon languish, The vine of Sibmah, Lords of nations did beat her choice vines, To Jazer they have come, They have wandered in a wilderness, Her plants have spread themselves, They have passed over a sea.
16.9: Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer, The vine of Sibmah, I water you with my tear, O Heshbon and Elealeh, For--for your summer fruits, and for your harvest, The shouting has fallen.
16.10: And removed have been gladness and joy from the fruitful field, And in vineyards they sing not, nor shout, Wine in the presses treads not the treader, Shouting I have caused to cease.
16.11: Therefore my bowels for Moab as a harp do sound, And my inward parts for Kir-Haresh.
16.12: And it has come to pass, when it has been seen, That weary has been Moab on the high place, And he has come to his sanctuary to pray, And is not able.
16.13: This is the word that Jehovah has spoken to Moab from that time,
16.14: And now has Jehovah spoken, saying, `In three years, as years of an hireling, Lightly esteemed is the honour of Moab, With all the great multitude, And the remnant is little, small, not mighty!'

17.1: The burden of Damascus. Indeed, Damascus is taken away from being a city, And it has been a heap--a ruin.
17.2: Forsaken are the cities of Aroer, For droves they are, and they have lain down, And there is none troubling.
17.3: And ceased has the fortress from Ephraim, And the kingdom from Damascus, And the remnant of Aram are as the honour of the sons of Israel, The affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts!
17.4: And it has come to pass, in that day, Wax poor does the honour of Jacob, And the fatness of his flesh does wax lean.
17.5: And it has come to pass, As the gathering by the reaper of the standing corn, And his arm the ears reaps, And it has come to pass, As the gathering of the ears in the valley of Rephaim,
17.6: And left in him have been gleanings, As the compassing of an olive, Two--three berries on the top of a branch, Four--five on the fruitful boughs, The affirmation of Jehovah, God of Israel!
17.7: In that day does man look to His Maker, Yes, his eyes to the Holy One of Israel look,
17.8: And he looks not to the altars. The work of his own hands, And that which his own fingers made He sees not--the shrines and the images.
17.9: In that day are the cities of his strength As the forsaken thing of the forest, And the branch that they have left, Because of the sons of Israel, It also has been a desolation.
17.10: Because you have forgotten the God of your salvation, And the rock of your strength have not remembered, Therefore you plant plants of pleasantness, And with a strange slip sow it,
17.11: In the day your plant you cause to become great, And in the morning your seed make to flourish, A heap is the harvest in a day of overflowing, And of mortal pain.
17.12: Woe to the multitude of many peoples, As the sounding of seas they sound; And to the wasting of nations, As the wasting of mighty waters they are wasted.
17.13: Nations as the wasting of many waters are wasted, And He has pushed against it, And it has fled afar off, And been pursued as chaff of hills before wind, And as a rolling thing before a hurricane.
17.14: At even-time, indeed, terror, before morning it is not, This is the portion of our spoilers, And the lot of our plunderers!

18.1: Ho, land shadowed with wings, That is beyond the rivers of Cush,
18.2: That is sending by sea ambassadors, Even with implements of reed on the face of the waters, --Go, you light messengers, To a nation drawn out and peeled, To a people fearful from its beginning and onwards, A nation meeting out by line, and treading down, Whose land floods have spoiled.
18.3: All you inhabitants of the world, And you dwellers of earth, At the lifting up of an ensign on hills you look, And at the blowing of a trumpet you hear.
18.4: For thus said Jehovah to me, `I rest, and I look on My settled place, As a clear heat on an herb. As a thick cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
18.5: For before harvest, when the flower is perfect, And the blossom is producing unripe fruit, Then has one cut the sprigs with pruning hooks, And the branches he has turned aside, cut down.
18.6: They are left together to the ravenous fowl of the mountains, And to the beast of the earth, And summered on them has the ravenous fowl, And every beast of the earth winters on them.
18.7: At that time brought is a present to Jehovah of Hosts, A nation drawn out and peeled. Even of a people fearful from the beginning hitherto, A nation meting out by line, and treading down, Whose land floods have spoiled, To the place of the name of Jehovah of Hosts--mount Zion!'

19.1: The burden of Egypt. Indeed, Jehovah is riding on a swift thick cloud, And He has entered Egypt, And moved have been the idols of Egypt at His presence, And the heart of Egypt melts in its midst.
19.2: And I armed Egyptians against Egyptians, And they fought, each against his brother, And each against his neighbour, City against city, kingdom against kingdom.
19.3: And emptied out has been in its midst the spirit of Egypt. And its counsel I swallow up, And they have sought to the idols, And to the charmers, And to those having familiar spirits, And to the wizards.
19.4: And I have delivered the Egyptians Into the hand of a hard lord, And a strong king does rule over them, An affirmation of the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts.
19.5: And failed have waters from the sea, And a river is wasted and dried up.
19.6: And they have turned away the flowings, Weak and dried up have been brooks of the bulwark, Reed and flag have withered.
19.7: Exposed things by the brook, by the edge of the brook, And every sown thing of the brook, has withered, It has been driven away, and is not.
19.8: And lamented have the fishers, And mourned have all casting angle into a brook, And those spreading nets on the face of the waters have languished.
19.9: And ashamed have been makers of fine flax, And weavers of net-works.
19.10: And its foundations have been smitten, All making wages are afflicted in soul.
19.11: Only, fools are the princes of Zoan, The counsel of the wise ones of the counsellors of Pharaoh has become brutish. How say you to Pharaoh, `A son of the wise am I, a son of kings of antiquity?'
19.12: Where are they now, your wise ones? Yes, let them tell to you, I pray you, And they know what Jehovah of Hosts has counselled against Egypt!
19.13: Foolish have been princes of Zoan, Lifted up have been princes of Noph, And they have caused Egypt to err, The chief of her tribes.
19.14: Jehovah has mingled in her midst A spirit of perverseness, And they have caused Egypt to err in all its work, As a drunkard errs in his vomit.
19.15: And there is no work to Egypt, That head or tail, branch or reed, may do.
19.16: In that day is Egypt like women, And it has mourned, and been afraid, Because of the waving of the hand of Jehovah of Hosts, That He is waving over it.
19.17: And the land of Judah has been to Egypt for a cause of staggering, Every one who does mention it, for himself fears, Because of the counsel of Jehovah of Hosts, That He is counselling against it.
19.18: In that day there are five cities in the land of Egypt, Speaking the lip of Canaan, And swearing to Jehovah of Hosts, `The city of destruction,' is said of one.
19.19: In that day there is an altar to Jehovah In the midst of the land of Egypt, And a standing pillar near its border to Jehovah,
19.20: And it has been for a sign and for a testimony, To Jehovah of Hosts in the land of Egypt, For they cry to Jehovah from the face of oppressors, And He sends to them a saviour, Even a great one, and has delivered them.
19.21: And known has been Jehovah to Egypt, And the Egyptians have known Jehovah in that day, And done sacrifice and present, And vowed a vow to Jehovah, and completed it.
19.22: And Jehovah has smitten Egypt, smiting and healing, And they have turned back to Jehovah, And He has been entreated of them, And has healed them.
19.23: In that day is a highway out of Egypt to Asshur, And come in have the Assyrians to Egypt, And the Egyptians into Asshur, And the Egyptians have served with the Assyrians.
19.24: In that day is Israel third, After Egypt, and after Asshur, A blessing in the heart of the earth.
19.25: In that Jehovah of Hosts did bless it, saying, `Blessed is My people--Egypt, And the work of My hands--Asshur, And My inheritance--Israel!'

20.1: In the year of the coming in of Tartan to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Asshur sends him, and he fights against Ashdod, and captures it,
20.2: at that time spoke Jehovah by the hand of Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, `Go, and you have loosed the sackcloth from off your loins, and your sandal you do draw from off your foot,' and he does so, going naked and barefoot.
20.3: And Jehovah says, `As My servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot three years, a sign and a wonder for Egypt and for Cush,
20.4: so does the king of Asshur lead the captivity of Egypt, and the removal of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with seat uncovered--the nakedness of Egypt;
20.5: and they have been affrighted and ashamed of Cush their confidence, and of Egypt their beauty,
20.6: and the inhabitant of this isle has said in that day--Indeed, thus is our trust, Where we have fled for help, To be delivered from the king of Asshur, And how do we escape--we?'

21.1: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. `Like hurricanes in the south for passing through, From the wilderness it has come, From a fearful land.
21.2: A hard vision has been declared to me, The treacherous dealer is dealing treacherously, And the destroyer is destroying. Go up, O Elam, besiege, O Media, All its sighing I have caused to cease.
21.3: Therefore filled have been my loins with great pain, Pangs have seized me as pangs of a travailing woman, I have been bent down by hearing, I have been troubled by seeing.
21.4: Wandered has my heart, trembling has terrified me, The twilight of my desire He has made a fear to me,
21.5: Arrange the table, watch in the watch-tower, Eat, drink, rise, you heads, anoint the shield,
21.6: For thus said the Lord to me: `Go, station the watchman, That which he sees let him declare.'
21.7: And he has seen a chariot--a couple of horsemen, The rider of an ass, the rider of a camel, And he has given attention--He has increased attention!
21.8: And he cries--a lion, `On a watch-tower my lord, I am standing continually by day, And on my ward I am stationed whole nights.
21.9: And indeed, this, the chariot of a man is coming, A couple of horsemen.' And he answers and says: `Fallen, fallen has Babylon, And all the graven images of her gods He has broken to the earth.
21.10: O my threshing, and the son of my floor, That which I heard from Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, I have declared to you!'
21.11: The burden of Dumah. To me is one calling from Seir `Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?'
21.12: The watchman has said, `Come has morning, and also night, If you inquire, inquire you, turn back, come.'
21.13: The burden on Arabia. In a forest in Arabia you lodge, O travellers of Dedanim.
21.14: To meet the thirsty brought water have Inhabitants of the land of Tema, With his bread they came before a fugitive.
21.15: For from the face of destructions they fled, From the face of a stretched-out sword, And from the face of a trodden bow, And from the face of the grievousness of battle.
21.16: For thus said the Lord to me: `Within a year, as years of a hireling, Consumed has been all the honour of Kedar.
21.17: And the remnant of the number of bow-men, The mighty of the sons of Kedar are few, For Jehovah, God of Israel, has spoken!'

22.1: The burden of the Valley of Vision. What--to you, now, that you have gone up, All of you--to the roofs?
22.2: Full of stirs--a noisy city--an exulting city, Your pierced are not pierced of the sword, Nor dead in battle.
22.3: All your rulers fled together from the bow, Bound have been all found of you, They have been kept bound together, Afar off they have fled.
22.4: Therefore I said, `Look you from me, I am bitter in my weeping, Haste not to comfort me, For the destruction of the daughter of my people.'
22.5: For a day of noise, and of treading down, And of perplexity, is to the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, In the valley of vision, digging down a wall, And crying to the mountain.
22.6: And Elam has borne a quiver, In a chariot of men--horsemen, And Kir has exposed a shield.
22.7: And it comes to pass, The choice of your valleys have been full of chariots, And the horsemen place themselves diligently at the gate.
22.8: And one removes the covering of Judah, And you look in that day To the armour of the house of the forest,
22.9: And the breaches of the city of David you have seen, For they have become many, And you gather the waters of the lower pool,
22.10: And the houses of Jerusalem you did number, And you break down the houses to fence the wall.
22.11: And a ditch you made between the two walls, For the waters of the old pool, And you have not looked to its Maker, And its Framer of old you have not seen.
22.12: And call does the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, In that day, to weeping and to lamentation, And to baldness and to girding on of sackcloth,
22.13: And indeed, joy and gladness, slaying of oxen, And slaughtering of sheep, Eating of flesh, and drinking of wine, Eat and drink, for to-morrow we die.
22.14: And revealed it has been in my ears, By Jehovah of Hosts: Not pardoned is this iniquity to you, Till you die, said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts.
22.15: Thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts: `Go, enter in to this steward, To Shebna, who is over the house:
22.16: What--to you here? And who--to you here? That you have hewn out to you here--a sepulchre? Hewing on high his sepulchre, Graving in a rock a dwelling for himself.
22.17: Indeed, Jehovah is casting you up and down, A casting up and down, O mighty one,
22.18: And your coverer covering, wrapping round, Wraps you round, O babbler, On a land broad of sides--there you die, And there the chariots of your honour Are the shame of the house of your lord.
22.19: And I have thrust you from your station, And from your office he throws you down.
22.20: And it has come to pass, in that day, That I have called to my servant, To Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
22.21: And I have clothed him with your coat, And with your girdle I strengthen him, And your garment I give into his hand, And he has been for a father to the inhabitant of Jerusalem, And to the house of Judah.
22.22: And I have placed the key Of the house of David on his shoulder, And he has opened, and none is shutting, And has shut, and none is opening.
22.23: And I have fixed him a nail in a stedfast place, And he has been for a throne of honour To the house of his father.
22.24: And they have hanged on him All the honour of the house of his father, The offspring and the issue, All vessels of small quality, From vessels of basins to all vessels of flagons.
22.25: In that day--an affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts, Moved is the nail that is fixed In a stedfast place, Yes, it has been cut down, and has fallen, And cut off has been the burden that is on it, For Jehovah has spoken!'

23.1: The Burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish, For it has been destroyed, Without house, without entrance, From the land of Chittim it was revealed to them.
23.2: Be silent, you inhabitants of the isle, Trader of Zidon, passing the sea, they filled you.
23.3: And in many waters is the seed of Sihor, The harvest of the brook is her increase, And she is a mart of nations.
23.4: Be ashamed, O Zidon; for the sea spoke, The strength of the sea, saying: `I have not been pained, nor have I brought forth, Nor have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins.'
23.5: As at the report of Egypt they are pained, So at the report of Tyre.
23.6: Pass over to Tarshish, howl, you inhabitants of the isle,
23.7: Is this your exulting one? From the days of old is her antiquity, Carry her do her own feet afar off to sojourn.
23.8: Who has counselled this against Tyre, The crowning one, whose traders are princes, Her merchants the honoured of earth?'
23.9: Jehovah of Hosts has counselled it, To pollute the excellency of all beauty, To make light all the honoured of earth.
23.10: Pass through your land as a brook, Daughter of Tarshish, there is no more a girdle.
23.11: His hand He has stretched out over the sea, He has caused kingdoms to tremble, Jehovah has charged concerning the merchant one, To destroy her strong places.
23.12: And He says, `You do not add any more to exult, O oppressed one, virgin daughter of Zidon, To Chittim arise, pass over, Even there--there is no rest for you.'
23.13: Indeed, the land of the Chaldeans--this people was not, Asshur founded it for the Ziim, They raised its watch-towers, They lifted up her palaces, --He has appointed her for a ruin!
23.14: Howl, you ships of Tarshish, For your strength has been destroyed.
23.15: And it has come to pass, in that day, That forgotten is Tyre seventy years, According to the days of one king. At the end of seventy years there is to Tyre as the song of the harlot.
23.16: Take a harp, go round the city, O forgotten harlot, play well, Multiply song that you may be remembered.
23.17: And it has come to pass, At the end of seventy years Jehovah inspects Tyre, And she has repented of her gift, That she committed fornication With all kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.
23.18: And her merchandise and her gift have been holy to Jehovah, Not treasured up nor stored, For to those sitting before Jehovah is her merchandise, To eat to satiety, and for a lasting covering!

24.1: Indeed, Jehovah is emptying the land, And is making it waste, And has overturned it on its face, And has scattered its inhabitants.
24.2: And it has been--as a people so a priest, As the servant so his master, As the maid-servant so her mistress, As the buyer so the seller, As the lender so the borrower, As the usurer so he who is lifting it on himself.
24.3: Utterly emptied is the land, and utterly spoiled, For Jehovah has spoken this word:
24.4: Mourned, faded has the land, Languished, faded has the world, Languished have they--the high place of the people of the land.
24.5: And the land has been defiled under its inhabitants, Because they have transgressed laws, They have changed a statute, They have made void a covenant age-during.
24.6: Therefore a curse has consumed the land, And the inhabitants in it are become desolate, Therefore consumed have been inhabitants of the land, And few men have been left.
24.7: Mourned has the new wine, languished the vine, Sighed have all the joyful of heart.
24.8: Ceased has the joy of tabrets, Ceased has the noise of exulting ones, Ceased has the joy of a harp.
24.9: With a song they drink not wine, Bitter is strong drink to those drinking it.
24.10: It was broken down--a city of emptiness, Shut has been every house from entrance.
24.11: A cry over the wine is in out-places, Darkened has been all joy, Removed has been the joy of the land.
24.12: Left in the city is desolation, And with wasting is the gate smitten.
24.13: When thus it is in the heart of the land, In the midst of the peoples, As the compassing of the olive, As gleanings when harvest has been finished,
24.14: They--they lift up their voice, They sing of the excellency of Jehovah, They have cried aloud from the sea.
24.15: Therefore in prosperity honour you Jehovah, In isles of the sea, the name of Jehovah, God of Israel.
24.16: From the skirt of the earth we heard songs, The desire of the righteous. And I say, `Leanness is to me, Leanness is to me, woe is to me.' Treacherous dealers dealt treacherously, Yes, treachery, treacherous dealers dealt treacherously.
24.17: Fear, and a snare, and a gin, Are on you, O inhabitant of the land.
24.18: And it has come to pass, He who is fleeing from the noise of the fear Does fall into the snare, And he who is coming up from the midst of the snare, Is captured by the gin, For windows on high have been opened, And shaken are foundations of the land.
24.19: Utterly broken down has been the land, Utterly broken has been the land, Utterly moved has been the land.
24.20: Stagger greatly does the land as a drunkard, And it has been moved as a lodge, And heavy on it has been its transgression, And it has fallen, and adds not to rise.
24.21: And it has come to pass, in that day, Jehovah lays a charge on the host of the high place in the high place, And on the kings of the land on the land.
24.22: And they have been gathered--A gathering of bound ones in a pit, And shut up they have been in a prison, And after a multitude of days are inspected.
24.23: And confounded has been the moon, And ashamed has been the sun, For reigned has Jehovah of Hosts In mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, And over-against His elders--honour!

25.1: O Jehovah, my God are You, I exalt You, I confess Your name, For You have done a wonderful thing, Counsels of old, stedfastness, O stedfast One.
25.2: For You did make of a city a heap, Of a fenced city a ruin, A high place of strangers from being a city, To the age it is not built.
25.3: Therefore honour You do a strong people, A city of the terrible nations fears You.
25.4: For You have been a stronghold for the poor, A stronghold for the needy in his distress, A refuge from storm, a shadow from heat, When the spirit of the terrible is as a storm--a wall.
25.5: As heat in a dry place, The noise of strangers You humble, Heat with the shadow of a thick cloud, The singing of the terrible is humbled.
25.6: And made has Jehovah of Hosts, For all the peoples in this mount, A banquet of fat things, a banquet of preserved things, Fat things full of marrow, preserved things refined.
25.7: And swallowed up has He in this mountain The face of the wrapping that is wrapped over all the peoples, And of the covering that is spread over all the nations.
25.8: He has swallowed up death in victory, And wiped has the Lord Jehovah, The tear from off all faces, And the reproach of His people He turns aside from off all the earth, For Jehovah has spoken.
25.9: And one has said in that day, `Indeed, this is our God, We waited for Him, and He saves us, This is Jehovah, we have waited for Him, We joy and rejoice in His salvation.'
25.10: For rest does the hand of Jehovah on this mountain, And trodden down is Moab under Him, As trodden down is straw on a dunghill.
25.11: And he spread out his hands in its midst, As spread out does the swimmer to swim; And He has humbled his excellency With the machinations of his hands.
25.12: And the fortress of the high place of your walls He has bowed down--He has made low, He has caused it to come to the earth, --to dust.

26.1: In that day sung is this song in the land of Judah: `We have a strong city, Salvation He does make walls and bulwark.
26.2: Open you the gates, that enter may a righteous nation, Preserving stedfastness.
26.3: An imagination supported You fortify peace--peace! For in You it is confident.
26.4: Trust you in Jehovah for ever, For in Jah Jehovah is a rock of ages,
26.5: For He bowed down the dwellers on high, A city set on high He makes low, He makes it low to the earth, He causes it to come to the dust,
26.6: Tread it down does a foot, Feet of the poor--steps of the weak.
26.7: The path for the righteous is uprightness, O upright One, The path of the righteous You do ponder.
26.8: Also, in the path of Your judgments, O Jehovah, we have waited for You, To Your name and to Your remembrance Is the desire of the soul.
26.9: With my soul I desired You in the night, Also, with my spirit within me I seek You earnestly, For when Your judgments are on the earth, The inhabitants of the world have learned righteousness.
26.10: The wicked finds favour, He has not learned righteousness, In a land of straightforwardness he deals perversely, And sees not the excellency of Jehovah.
26.11: O Jehovah, high is Your hand--they see not, They see the zeal of the people, and are ashamed, Also, the fire--Your adversaries, consumes them.
26.12: O Jehovah, You appoint peace to us, For, all our works also You have worked for us.
26.13: O Jehovah our God, lords have ruled us besides You, Only, by You we make mention of Your name.
26.14: Dead--they live not, Rephaim, they rise not, Therefore You have inspected and do destroy them, Yes, you destroy all their memory.
26.15: You have added to the nation, O Jehovah, You have added to the nation, You have been honoured, You have put far off all the ends of earth.
26.16: O Jehovah, in distress they missed You, They have poured out a whisper, Your chastisement is on them.
26.17: When a pregnant woman comes near to the birth, She is pained--she cries in her pangs, So we have been from Your face, O Jehovah.
26.18: We have conceived, we have been pained. We have brought forth as it were wind, Salvation we do not work in the earth, Nor do the inhabitants of the world fall.
26.19: `Your dead live--My dead body they rise. Awake and sing, you dwellers in the dust, For the dew of herbs is your dew, And the land of Rephaim you cause to fall.
26.20: Come, My people, enter into your inner chambers, And shut your doors behind you, Hide yourself shortly a moment till the indignation pass over.
26.21: For, indeed, Jehovah is coming out of His place, To charge the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth upon him, And revealed has the earth her blood, Nor does she cover any more her slain!'

27.1: In that day lay a charge does Jehovah, With his sword--the sharp, and the great, and the strong, On leviathan--a fleeing serpent, And on leviathan--a crooked serpent, And He has slain the dragon that is in the sea.
27.2: In that day, `A desirable vineyard,' respond you to her,
27.3: I, Jehovah, am its keeper, every moment I water it, Lest any lay a charge against it, Night and day I keep it!
27.4: Fury is not in Me; Who gives Me a brier--a thorn in battle? I step into it, I burn it at once.
27.5: Or--he does take hold on My strength, He does make peace with Me, Peace he does make with Me.
27.6: Those coming in He causes to take root, Jacob does blossom, and flourished has Israel, And they have filled the face of the world with increase.
27.7: As the smiting of his smiter has He smitten him? As the slaying of his slain does He slay?
27.8: In measure, in sending it forth, you strive with it, He has taken away by His sharp wind, In the day of an east wind,
27.9: Therefore by this is the iniquity of Jacob covered, And this is all the fruit--To take away his sin, in His setting all the stones of an altar, As chalkstones beaten in pieces, They rise not--shrines and images.
27.10: For the fenced city is alone, A habitation cast out and forsaken as a wilderness, There does the calf delight, And there it lies down, And has consumed its branches.
27.11: In the withering of its branch it is broken off, Women are coming in setting it on fire, For it is not a people of understanding, Therefore pity it not does its Maker, And its Former does not favour it.
27.12: And it has come to pass, in that day, Beat out does Jehovah from the branch of the river, To the stream of Egypt, And you are gathered one by one, O sons of Israel.
27.13: And it has come to pass, in that day, It is blown with a great trumpet, And come in have those perishing in the land of Asshur, And those cast out in the land of Egypt, And have bowed themselves to Jehovah, In the holy mount--in Jerusalem!

28.1: Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim. And the fading flower of the beauty of his glory, That is on the head of the fat valley of the broken down of wine.
28.2: Indeed, a mighty and strong one is to the Lord, As a storm of hail--a destructive shower, As an inundation of mighty waters overflowing, He cast down to the earth with the hand.
28.3: By feet trodden down is the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim,
28.4: And the fading flower of the beauty of his glory That is on the head of the fat valley, Has been as its first-fruit before summer, That its beholder sees, While it is yet in his hand he swallows it.
28.5: In that day is Jehovah of Hosts For a crown of beauty, and for a diadem of glory, To the remnant of His people.
28.6: And for a spirit of judgment To him who is sitting in the judgment, And for might to those turning back the battle to the gate.
28.7: And even these through wine have erred, And through strong drink have wandered, Priest and prophet erred through strong drink, They have been swallowed up of the wine, They wandered because of the strong drink, They have erred in seeing, They have stumbled judicially.
28.8: For all tables have been full of vomit, Filth--without place!
28.9: By whom does He teach knowledge? And by whom does He cause to understand the report? The weaned from milk, the removed from breasts,
28.10: For rule is on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, A little here, a little there,
28.11: For by scorned lip, and by another tongue, Does He speak to this people.
28.12: To whom He has said, `This is the rest, give you rest to the weary, And this--the refreshing:' And they have not been willing to hear,
28.13: And to whom a word of Jehovah has been, Rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, A little here, a little there, So that they go and have stumbled backward, And been broken, and snared, and captured.
28.14: Therefore, hear a word of Jehovah, you men of scorning, Ruling this people that is in Jerusalem.
28.15: Because you have said: `We have made a covenant with death, And with Sheol we have made a provision, An overflowing scourge, when it passes over, Does not meet us, Though we have made a lie our refuge, And in falsehood have been hidden.'
28.16: Therefore, thus said the Lord Jehovah: `Indeed, I am laying a foundation in Zion, A stone--a tried stone, a corner stone precious, a settled foundation, He who is believing does not make haste.
28.17: And I have put judgment for a line, And righteousness for a plummet, And sweep away does hail the refuge of lies, And the secret hiding-place do waters overflow.
28.18: And disannulled has been your covenant with death, And your provision with Sheol does not stand, An overflowing scourge, when it passes over, Then you have been to it for a treading-place.
28.19: From the fulness of its passing over it takes you, For morning by morning it passes over, By day and by night, And it has been only a trembling to consider the report.
28.20: For shorter has been the bed Than to stretch one's self out in, And the covering has been narrower Than to wrap one's self up in.
28.21: For as at mount Perazim rise does Jehovah, As at the valley in Gibeon He is troubled, To do His work--strange is His work, And to do His deed--strange is His deed.'
28.22: And now, show not yourselves scorners, Lest strong be your bands, For a consumption, that is determined, I have heard, by the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is for all the land.
28.23: Give ear, and hear my voice, Attend, and hear my saying:
28.24: The whole day ploughs the ploughman to sow? He opens and harrows his ground!
28.25: Has he not, if he have made level its face, Then scattered fitches, and cummin sprinkle, And has placed the principal wheat, And the appointed barley, And the rie in its own border?
28.26: And instruct him for judgment does his God, He does direct him.
28.27: For not with a sharp-pointed thing threshed are fitches, And the wheel of a cart on cummin turned round, For with a staff beaten out are fitches, And cummin with a rod.
28.28: Bread- corn is beaten small, For not for ever does he sorely thresh it, Nor crushed it has a wheel of his cart, Nor do his hoofs beat it small.
28.29: Even this from Jehovah of Hosts has gone out, He has made counsel wonderful, He has made wisdom great!

29.1: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, The city of the encampment of David! Add year to year, let festivals go round.
29.2: And I have sent distress to Ariel, And it has been lamentation and mourning, And it has been to me as Ariel.
29.3: And I encamped, O babbler, against you, And I laid siege against you--a camp. And I raised up against you bulwarks.
29.4: And you have been low, From the earth you speak, And from the dust make your saying low, And your voice has been from the earth, As one having a familiar spirit, And from the dust your saying whisper,
29.5: And as small dust has been The multitude of those scattering you, And as chaff passing on the multitude of the terrible, And it has been at an instant--suddenly.
29.6: By Jehovah of Hosts you are inspected, With thunder, and with an earthquake, And great noise, hurricane, and whirlwind, And flame of devouring fire.
29.7: And as a dream, a vision of night, has been The multitude of all the nations Who are warring against Ariel, And all its warriors, and its bulwark, Even of those distressing her.
29.8: And it has been, as when the hungry dreams, And indeed, he is eating, And he has waked, and empty is his soul, And as when the thirsty dreams, And indeed, he is drinking, and he has waked, And indeed, he is weary, and his soul is longing, So is the multitude of all the nations Who are warring against mount Zion.
29.9: Tarry and wonder, look you, yes, look, Be drunk, and not with wine, Stagger, and not with strong drink.
29.10: For poured out on you has Jehovah a spirit of deep sleep, And He closes your eyes--the prophets, And your heads--the seers--He covered.
29.11: And the vision of the whole is to you, As words of the sealed book, That they give to one knowing books, Saying, `Read this, we pray you,' And he has said, `I am not able, for it is sealed;'
29.12: And the book is given to him who has not known books, Saying, `Read this, we pray you,' And he has said, `I have not known books.'
29.13: And the Lord says: Because drawn near has this people, with its mouth, And with its lips they have honoured Me, And its heart it has put far off from Me, And their fear of Me is--A precept of men is taught!
29.14: Therefore, indeed, I am adding to do wonderfully with this people, A wonder, and a marvel, And perished has the wisdom of its wise ones, And the understanding of its intelligent ones hides itself.'
29.15: Woe to those going deep from Jehovah to hide counsel, And whose works have been in darkness. And they say, `Who is seeing us? And who is knowing us?'
29.16: Your perversion! as clay is the potter esteemed? That the work says of its maker, `He has not made me?' And the framed thing said of its framer, `He did not understand?'
29.17: Is it not yet a very little, And turned has Lebanon to a fruitful field, And the fruitful field for a forest is reckoned?
29.18: And heard in that day have the deaf the words of a book, And out of thick darkness, and out of darkness, The eyes of the blind do see.
29.19: And the humble have added joy in Jehovah, And the poor among men In the Holy One of Israel rejoice.
