29.20: For ceased has the terrible one, And consumed has been the scorner, And cut off have been all watching for iniquity,
29.21: Causing men to sin in word, And for a reprover in the gate lay a snare, And turn aside into emptiness the righteous.
29.22: Therefore, thus said Jehovah, Who ransomed Abraham, Concerning the house of Jacob: `Not now ashamed is Jacob, Nor now does his face become pale,
29.23: For in his seeing his children, The work of My hand, in his midst, They sanctify My name, And have sanctified the Holy One of Jacob, And the God of Israel they declare fearful.
29.24: And the erring in spirit have known understanding, And murmurers learn doctrine!'

30.1: Woe to apostate sons, The affirmation of Jehovah! To do counsel, and not from Me, And to spread out a covering, and not of My spirit, So as to add sin to sin.
30.2: Who are walking to go down to Egypt, And My mouth have not asked, To be strong in the strength of Pharaoh, And to trust in the shadow of Egypt.
30.3: And the strength of Pharaoh Has been to you for shame, And the trust in the shadow of Egypt confusion,
30.4: For in Zoan were his princes, And his messengers reach Hanes.
30.5: All he made ashamed of a people that profit not, Neither for help, not for profit, But for shame, and also for reproach!
30.6: The burden of the beasts of the south. Into a land of adversity and distress, Of young lion and of old lion, From where are viper and flying saraph, They carry on the shoulder of asses their wealth, And on the hump of camels their treasures, To a people not profitable.
30.7: Yes, Egyptians are vanity, and in vain do help, Therefore I have cried concerning this: `Their strength is to sit still.'
30.8: No, go in, write it on a tablet with them, And on a book engrave it, And it is for a latter day, for a witness to the age,
30.9: That a rebellious people is this, sons--liars, Sons not willing to hear the law of Jehovah.
30.10: Who have said to seers, `You do not see,' And to prophets, `You do not prophesy to us Straightforward things, Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits,
30.11: Turn aside from the way, decline from the path, Cause to cease from before us the Holy One of Israel.'
30.12: Therefore, thus said the Holy One of Israel, Because of your kicking against this word, And you trust in oppression, And perverseness, and rely on it,
30.13: Therefore is this iniquity to you as a breach falling, Swelled out in a wall set on high, Whose destruction suddenly, at an instant comes.
30.14: And He has broken it As the breaking of the potters' bottle, Beaten down--He does not spare, Nor is there found, in its beating down, A potsherd to take fire from the burning, And to draw out waters from a ditch.
30.15: For thus said the Lord Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel: `In returning and rest you are saved, In keeping quiet and in confidence is your might, And you have not been willing.
30.16: And you say, No, for on a horse we flee? Therefore you flee, And on the swift we ride! Therefore swift are your pursuers.
30.17: One thousand because of the rebuke of one, Because of the rebuke of five you flee, Till you have been surely left as a pole On the top of the mountain, And as an ensign on the height.
30.18: And therefore does wait Jehovah to favour you, And therefore He is exalted to pity you, For a God of judgment is Jehovah, O the blessedness of all waiting for Him.
30.19: For the people in Zion dwell in Jerusalem, Weep you not, weeping, Pitying, He pities you at the voice of your cry, When He hears He answers you.
30.20: And the Lord has given to you bread of adversity, And water of oppression. And your directors remove no more, And your eyes have seen your directors,
30.21: And your ear hears a word behind you, Saying, `This is the way, go you in it,' When you turn to the right, And when you turn to the left.
30.22: And you have defiled the covering of Your graven images of silver, And the ephod of your molten image of gold, You scatter them as a sickening thing, `Go out,' you say to it.
30.23: And He has given rain for your seed, With which you do sow the ground, And bread, the increase of the ground, And it has been fat and plenteous, Enjoy do your cattle in that day an enlarged pasture.
30.24: And the oxen and the young asses serving the ground, Fermented provender do eat, That one is winnowing with shovel and fan.
30.25: And there has been on every high mount, And on every exalted hill, Rivulets--streams of waters, In a day of much slaughter, in the falling of towers.
30.26: And the light of the moon has been as the light of the sun, And the light of the sun is sevenfold, As the light of seven days, In the day of Jehovah's binding up the breach of His people, When the stroke of its wound He heals.
30.27: Indeed, the name of Jehovah is coming from far, Burning is His anger, and great the flame, His lips have been full of indignation, And His tongue is as a devouring fire.
30.28: And His breath is as an overflowing stream, To the neck it divides, To sift nations with a sieve of vanity, And a bridle causing to err, Is on the jaws of the peoples.
30.29: Singing is to you as in a night sanctified for a festival, And joy of heart as he who is going with a pipe, To go in to the mountain of Jehovah, To the rock of Israel.
30.30: And caused to be heard has Jehovah The honour of His voice, And the coming down of His arm He does show with the raging of anger, And the flame of a consuming fire, Scattering, and inundation, and hailstone.
30.31: For from the voice of Jehovah broken down is Asshur, With a rod He smites.
30.32: And every passage of the settled staff, That Jehovah causes to rest on him, Has been with tabrets, and with harps, And in battles of shaking he has fought with it.
30.33: For, arranged from former time is Tophet, Even it for the king is prepared, He has made deep, He has made large, Its pile is fire and much wood, The breath of Jehovah, As a stream of brim stone, is burning in it!

31.1: Woe to those going down to Egypt for help, And on horses lean, And trust on chariots, because many, And on horsemen, because very strong, And have not looked on the Holy One of Israel, And Jehovah have not sought.
31.2: And He also is wise, and brings in evil, And His words He has not turned aside, And He has risen against a house of evil doers, And against the help of workers of iniquity.
31.3: And the Egyptians are men, and not God, And their horses are flesh, and not spirit, And Jehovah stretches out His hand, And stumbled has the helper, And fallen has the helped one, And together all of them are consumed.
31.4: For thus said Jehovah to me: `As growl does the lion and the young lion over his prey, Called against whom is a multitude of shepherds, From their voice he is not affrighted, And from their noise he is not humbled; So come down does Jehovah of Hosts To war on mount Zion, and on her height.
31.5: As birds flying, so does Jehovah of Hosts Cover over Jerusalem, covering and delivering, Passing over, and causing to escape.'
31.6: Turn back to Him from whom sons of Israel Have deepened apostasy.
31.7: For in that day despise does each His idols of silver, and his idols of gold, That your hands made to you--a sin.
31.8: And fallen has Asshur by sword, not of the high, Yes, a sword--not of the low, does consume him, And he has fled for himself from the face of a sword, And his young men become tributary.
31.9: And to his rock from fear he passes on, And affrighted by the ensign have been his princes--an affirmation of Jehovah, Who has a light in Zion, And who has a furnace in Jerusalem!

32.1: Indeed, for righteousness does a king reign, As to princes, for judgment they rule.
32.2: And each has been as a hiding-place from wind, And as a secret hiding-place from inundation, As rivulets of waters in a dry place, As a shadow of a heavy rock in a weary land.
32.3: And not dazzled are the eyes of beholders, And the ears of hearers do attend.
32.4: And the heart of those hastened Understands to know, And the tongue of stammerers hastes to speak clearly.
32.5: A fool is no more called `noble,' And to a miser it is not said, `rich;'
32.6: For a fool speaks folly, And his heart does iniquity, to do profanity, And to speak concerning Jehovah error, To empty the soul of the hungry, Yes, drink of the thirsty he causes to lack.
32.7: And the miser--his instruments are evil, He has counselled wicked devices, To corrupt the poor with lying sayings, Even when the needy speaks justly.
32.8: And the noble counselled noble things, And he for noble things rises up.
32.9: Women, easy ones, rise, hear my voice, Daughters, confident ones, give ear to my saying,
32.10: Days and a year you are troubled, O confident ones, For consumed has been harvest, The gathering comes not.
32.11: Tremble you women, you easy ones, Be troubled, you confident ones, Strip and make bare, with a girdle on the loins,
32.12: For breasts they are lamenting, For fields of desire, for the fruitful vine.
32.13: Over the ground of my people thorn--brier goes up, Surely over all houses of joy of the exulting city,
32.14: Surely the palace has been left, The multitude of the city forsaken, Fort and watch-tower has been for dens to the age, A joy of wild asses--a pasture of herds;
32.15: Till emptied out on us is the Spirit from on high, And a wilderness has become a fruitful field, And the fruitful field for a forest is reckoned.
32.16: And dwelt in the wilderness has judgment, And righteousness in the fruitful field remains.
32.17: And a work of the righteousness has been peace, And a service of the righteousness--Keeping quiet and confidence to the age.
32.18: And dwelt has My people in a peaceful habitation, And in stedfast tabernacles, And in quiet resting-places.
32.19: And it has hailed in the going down of the forest, And in the valley is the city low.
32.20: Happy are you sowing by all waters, Sending forth the foot of the ox and the ass!

33.1: Woe, spoiler! and you not spoiled, And treacherous! and they dealt not treacherously with you, When you do finish, O spoiler, you are spoiled, When you do finish dealing treacherously, They deal treacherously with you.
33.2: O Jehovah, favour us, for you we have waited, Be their arm, in the mornings, Yes, our salvation in time of adversity.
33.3: From the voice of a multitude fled have peoples, From your exaltation scattered have been nations.
33.4: And gathered has been your spoil, A gathering of the caterpillar, As a running to and fro of locusts is he running on it.
33.5: Set on high is Jehovah, for He is dwelling on high, He filled Zion with judgment and righteousness,
33.6: And has been the stedfastness of your times, The strength of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge, Fear of Jehovah--it is His treasure.
33.7: Indeed, `Their Ariel,' they have cried without, Messengers of peace do weep bitterly.
33.8: Desolated have been highways, Ceased has he who passes along the path, He has broken covenant, He has despised enemies, He has not esteemed a man.
33.9: Mourned, languished has the land, Confounded has been Lebanon, Withered has been Sharon as a wilderness, And shaking are Bashan and Carmel.
33.10: Now, do I arise, says Jehovah, Now I am exalted, now I am lifted up.
33.11: You conceive chaff, you bear stubble, Your spirit! --fire devours you.
33.12: And peoples have been as burnings of lime, Thorns, as sweepings, with fire they burn.
33.13: Hear, you far off, that which I have done, And know, you near ones, My might.
33.14: Afraid in Zion have been sinners, Seized has trembling the profane: Who does dwell for us--consuming fire, Who does dwell for us--burnings of the age?
33.15: Whoever is walking righteously, And is speaking uprightly, Kicking against gain of oppressions, Shaking his hands from taking hold on a bribe, Stopping his ear from hearing of blood, And shutting his eyes from looking on evil,
33.16: He high places does inhabit, Strongholds of rock are his high tower, His bread has been given, his waters stedfast.
33.17: A king in his beauty, see do your eyes, They see a land afar off.
33.18: Your heart does meditate terror, Where is he who is counting? Where is he who is weighing? Where is he who is counting the towers?
33.19: The strong people you see not, A people deeper of lip than to be understood, Of a scorned tongue, there is no understanding.
33.20: See Zion, the city of our meetings, Your eyes see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, A tent not taken down, Not removed are its pins for ever, And none of its cords are broken.
33.21: But there mighty is Jehovah for us, A place of rivers--streams broad of sides, No ship with oars does go into it, And a mighty ship does not pass over it.
33.22: For Jehovah our judge, Jehovah our lawgiver, Jehovah our king--He does save us.
33.23: Left have been your ropes, They strengthen not rightly their mast, They have not spread out a sail, Then apportioned has been a prey of much spoil, The lame have taken spoil.
33.24: Nor does an inhabitant say, `I was sick,' The people that is dwelling in it, is forgiven of iniquity!

34.1: Come near, you nations, to hear, And you peoples, give attention, Hear does the earth and its fulness, The world, and all its productions.
34.2: For wrath is to Jehovah against all the nations, And fury against all their host, He has devoted them to destruction, He has given them to slaughter.
34.3: And their wounded are cast out, And their carcases cause their stench to ascend, And melted have been mountains from their blood.
34.4: And consumed have been all the host of the heavens, And rolled together as a book have been the heavens, And all their hosts do fade, As the fading of a leaf of a vine, And as the fading one of a fig-tree.
34.5: For soaked in the heavens was My sword, Indeed, on Edom it comes down, On the people of My curse for judgment.
34.6: A sword is to Jehovah--it has been full of blood, It has been made fat with fatness, With blood of lambs and he-goats. With fat of kidneys of rams, For a sacrifice is to Jehovah in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
34.7: And come down have reems with them, And bullocks with bulls, And soaked has been their land from blood, And their dust from fatness is made fat.
34.8: (For a day of vengeance is to Jehovah, A year of recompences for Zion's strife,)
34.9: And turned have been her streams to pitch, And her dust to brimstone, And her land has become burning pitch.
34.10: By night and by day she is not quenched, To the age go up does her smoke, From generation to generation she is waste, For ever and ever, none is passing into her.
34.11: And possess her do pelican and hedge-hog, And owl and raven dwell in her, And He has stretched out over her A line of vacancy, and stones of emptiness.
34.12: To the kingdom her freemen they call, But there are none there, And all her princes are at an end.
34.13: And gone up her palaces have thorns, Nettle and bramble are in her fortresses, And it has been a habitation of dragons, A court for daughters of an ostrich.
34.14: And met have Ziim with Aiim, And the goat for its companion calls, Only there rested has the night-owl, And has found for herself a place of rest.
34.15: There made her nest has the bittern, Yes, she lays, and has hatched, And has gathered under her shadow, Only there gathered have been vultures, Each with its companion.
34.16: Seek out of the book of Jehovah, and read, One of these has not been lacking, None has missed its companion, For My mouth--it has commanded, And His spirit--He has gathered them.
34.17: And He has cast for them a lot, And His hand has apportioned it to them by line, To the age they possess it, To all generations they dwell in it!

35.1: They joy from the wilderness and dry place, And rejoice does the desert, and flourish as the rose,
35.2: Flourishing it does flourish, and rejoice, Yes, with joy and singing, The honour of Lebanon has been given to it, The beauty of Carmel and Sharon, They--they see the honour of Jehovah, The majesty of our God.
35.3: Strengthen you the feeble hands, Yes, the stumbling knees strengthen.
35.4: Say to the hastened of heart, `Be strong, Fear not, indeed, your God; vengeance comes, The recompence of God, He Himself does come and save you.'
35.5: Then opened are eyes of the blind, And ears of the deaf are unstopped,
35.6: Then leap as a hart does the lame, And sing does the tongue of the dumb, For broken up in a wilderness have been waters, And streams in a desert.
35.7: And the mirage has become a pond, And the thirsty land fountains of waters, In the habitation of dragons, Its place of couching down, a court for reed and rush.
35.8: And a highway has been there, and a way, And the `way of holiness' is called to it, Not pass over it does the unclean, And He Himself is by them, Whoever is going in the way--even fools err not.
35.9: No lion is there, yes, a destructive beast Ascends it not, it is not found there, And walked have the redeemed,
35.10: And the ransomed of Jehovah return, And have entered Zion with singing. And joy age-during on their head, Joy and gladness they attain, And fled away have sorrow and sighing!

36.1: And it comes to pass, in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, come up has Sennacherib king of Asshur against all the fenced cities of Judah, and seizes them.
36.2: And the king of Asshur sends Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to the king Hezekiah, with a heavy force, and he stands by the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller's field,
36.3: and go forth to him does Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who is over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the remembrancer.
36.4: And Rabshakeh says to them, `Say you, I pray you, to Hezekiah, `Thus said the great king, the king of Asshur, What is this confidence in which you have confided?
36.5: I have said: Only, a word of the lips! counsel and might are for battle: now, on whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?
36.6: `Indeed, you have trusted on the staff of this broken reed--on Egypt--which a man leans on, and it has gone into his hand, and pierced it--so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all those trusting on him.
36.7: `And do you say to me, To Jehovah our God we have trusted? is it not He, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has turned aside, and says to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar you do bow yourselves?
36.8: `And now, negotiate, I pray you, with my lord the king of Asshur, and I give to you two thousand horses, if you are able to put for you riders on them.
36.9: And how do you turn back the face of one captain of the least of the servants of my lord, and do trust for you on Egypt, for chariot and for horsemen?
36.10: And now, without Jehovah have I come up against this land to destroy it? Jehovah said to me, Go up to this land, and you have destroyed it.'
36.11: And Eliakim says--and Shebna and Joah--to Rabshakeh, `Speak, we pray you, to your servants in Aramaean, for we are understanding; and do not speak to us in Jewish, in the ears of the people who are on the wall.'
36.12: And Rabshakeh says, `To your lord, and to you, has my lord sent me to speak these words? is it not for the men--those sitting on the wall to eat their own dung and to drink their own water with you?'
36.13: And Rabshakeh stands and calls with a great voice in Jewish, and says, `Hear you the words of the great king, the king of Asshur:
36.14: Thus said the king, Let not Hezekiah lift you up, for he is not able to deliver you;
36.15: and let not Hezekiah make you trust to Jehovah, saying, Jehovah does certainly deliver us, this city is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.
36.16: `Do not hearken to Hezekiah, for thus said the king of Asshur, Make you with me a blessing, and come out to me, and eat you each of his vine, and each of his fig-tree, and drink you each the waters of his own well,
36.17: till my coming in, and I have taken you to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards;
36.18: lest Hezekiah does persuade you, saying, Jehovah does deliver us. `Have the gods of the nations delivered each his land out of the hand of the king of Asshur?
36.19: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where the gods of Sepharvaim, that they have delivered Samaria out of my hand?
36.20: Who among all the gods of these lands are they who have delivered their land out of my hand, that Jehovah does deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'
36.21: And they keep silent, and have not answered him a word, for a command of the king is, saying, `Do not answer him.'
36.22: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who is over the house, comes in, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the remembrancer, to Hezekiah with rent garments, and they declare to him the words of Rabshakeh.

37.1: And it comes to pass, at the king Hezekiah's hearing, that he rends his garments, and covers himself with sackcloth, and enters the house of Jehovah,
37.2: and sends Eliakim, who is over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet,
37.3: and they say to him, `Thus said Hezekiah, A day of distress, and rebuke, and despising, is this day; for come have sons to the birth, and power there is not to bear.
37.4: `It may be Jehovah your God does hear the words of Rabshakeh with which the king of Asshur his lord has sent him to reproach the living God, and has decided concerning the words that Jehovah your God has heard, and you have lifted up prayer for the remnant that is found.'
37.5: And the servants of king Hezekiah come in to Isaiah,
37.6: and Isaiah says to them, `Thus do you say to your lord, Thus said Jehovah, Be not afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Asshur have reviled Me.
37.7: Indeed, I am giving in him a spirit, and he has heard a report, and has turned back to his land, and I have caused him to fall by the sword in his land.'
37.8: And Rabshakeh turns back and finds the king of Asshur fighting against Libnah, for he has heard that he has journeyed from Lachish.
37.9: And he hears concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, `He has come out to fight with you;' and he hears, and sends messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
37.10: `Thus do you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not your God lift you up in whom you are trusting, saying, Jerusalem is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.
37.11: Indeed, you have heard that which the kings of Asshur have done to all the lands--to devote them--and you are delivered!
37.12: Did the gods of the nations deliver them whom my fathers destroyed--Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden, who are in Telassar?
37.13: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'
37.14: And Hezekiah takes the letters out of the hand of the messengers, and reads them, and Hezekiah goes up to the house of Jehovah, and Hezekiah spreads it before Jehovah.
37.15: And Hezekiah prays to Jehovah, saying,
37.16: `Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, inhabiting the cherubs, You are God Himself--Yourself alone--to all kingdoms of the earth, You have made the heavens and the earth.
37.17: Incline, O Jehovah, Your ear, and hear; open, O Jehovah, Your eyes and see; and hear You all the words of Sennacherib that he has sent to reproach the living God.
37.18: `Truly, O Jehovah, kings of Asshur have laid waste all the lands and their land,
37.19: so as to put their gods into fire--for they are no gods, but work of the hands of man, wood and stone--and they destroy them.
37.20: And now, Jehovah our God, save us from his hand, and all kingdoms of the earth do know that You are Jehovah, Yourself alone.'
37.21: And Isaiah son of Amoz sends to Hezekiah, saying, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, That which you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Asshur--
37.22: this is the word that Jehovah spoke concerning him: Trampled on you, laughed at you, Has the virgin daughter of Zion, Behind you shaken the head has the daughter of Jerusalem.
37.23: Whom have you reproached and reviled? And against whom lifted up the voice? Yes, you do lift up on high your eyes Against the Holy One of Israel.
37.24: By the hand of your servants You have reviled the Lord, and say: In the multitude of my chariots I have come up to a high place of hills, The sides of Lebanon, And I cut down the height of its cedars, The choice of its firs, And I enter the high place of its extremity, The forest of its Carmel.
37.25: I--I have dug and drunk waters, And I dry up with the sole of my steps All floods of a bulwark.
37.26: Have you not heard from afar? --it I did, From days of old--that I formed it. Now, I have brought it in, And it is to make desolate, Ruinous heaps--fenced cities,
37.27: And their inhabitants are feeble-handed, They were broken down, and are dried up. They have been the herb of the field, And the greenness of the tender grass, Grass of the roofs, And blasted corn, before it has risen up.
37.28: And your sitting down, and your going out, And your coming in, I have known, And your anger toward Me.
37.29: Because of your anger toward Me, And your noise--it came up into My ears, I have put My hook in your nose, And My bridle in your lips, And I have caused you to turn back In the way in which you came.
37.30: --And this to you is the sign, Food of the year is self-sown grain, And in the second year the spontaneous growth, And in the third year, sow you and reap, And plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
37.31: And it has continued--the escaped Of the house of Judah that has been left--To take root beneath, And it has made fruit upward.
37.32: For from Jerusalem goes forth a remnant, And an escape from mount Zion, The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts does this.
37.33: Therefore, thus said Jehovah, Concerning the king of Asshur: He does not come in to this city, Nor does he shoot there an arrow, Nor does he come before it with shield, Nor does he pour out against it a mount.
37.34: In the way that he came, in it he turns back, And to this city he does not come in, An affirmation of Jehovah,
37.35: And I have covered over this city, To save it, for My own sake, And for the sake of David My servant.'
37.36: And a messenger of Jehovah goes out, and smites in the camp of Asshur a hundred and eighty and five thousand; and men rise early in the morning, and indeed, all of them are dead corpses.
37.37: And journey, and go, and turn back does Sennacherib king of Asshur, and dwells in Nineveh.
37.38: And it comes to pass, he is bowing himself in the house of Nisroch his god, and Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons have smitten him with the sword, and they have escaped to the land of Ararat, and Esar-Haddon his son reigns in his stead.

38.1: In those days has Hezekiah been sick to death, and come in to him does Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, and says to him, `Thus said Jehovah: Give a charge to your house, for you are dying, and do not live.'
38.2: And Hezekiah turns round his face to the wall, and prays to Jehovah,
38.3: and says, `I pray you, O Jehovah, remember, I pray You, how I have walked habitually before You in truth, and with a perfect heart, and that which is good in your eyes I have done;' and Hezekiah weeps--a great weeping.
38.4: And a word of Jehovah is to Isaiah, saying,
38.5: Go, and you have said to Hezekiah, Thus said Jehovah, God of David your father, `I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tear, indeed, I am adding to your days fifteen years,
38.6: and out of the hand of the king of Asshur I deliver you and this city, and have covered over this city.
38.7: And this is to you the sign from Jehovah, that Jehovah does this thing that He has spoken.
38.8: Indeed, I am bringing back the shadow of the degrees that it has gone down on the degrees of Ahaz, by the sun, backward ten degrees:' and the sun turns back ten degrees in the degrees that it had gone down.
38.9: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah concerning his being sick, when he revives from his sickness:
38.10: `I--I said in the cutting off of my days, I go in to the gates of Sheol, I have numbered the remnant of my years.
38.11: I said, I do not see Jah--Jah! In the land of the living, I do not behold man any more, With the inhabitants of the world.
38.12: My sojourning has departed, And been removed from me as a shepherd's tent, I have drawn together, as a weaver, my life, By weakness it cuts me off, From day to night You do end me.
38.13: I have set Him till morning as a lion, So does He break all my bones, From day to night You do end me.
38.14: As a crane--a swallow--so I chatter, I mourn as a dove, Drawn up have been my eyes on high, O Jehovah, oppression is on me, be my surety.
38.15: --What do I say? seeing He said to me, And He Himself has worked, I go softly all my years for the bitterness of my soul.
38.16: Lord, by these do men live, And by all in them is the life of my spirit, And You save me, make me also to live,
38.17: Indeed, to peace He changed for me bitterness, And You have delighted in my soul without corruption, For You have cast behind Your back all my sins.
38.18: For Sheol does not confess You, Death does not praise You, Those going down to the pit hope not for Your truth.
38.19: The living, the living, he does confess You.
38.20: Like myself to-day--a father to sons Does make known of Your faithfulness, O Jehovah--to save me: And my songs we sing all days of our lives In the house of Jehovah.'
38.21: And Isaiah says, `Let them take a bunch of figs, and plaster over the ulcer, and he lives.'
38.22: And Hezekiah says, `What is the sign that I go up to the house of Jehovah!'

39.1: At that time has Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, when he hears that he has been sick, and is become strong.
39.2: And Hezekiah rejoices over them, and shows them the house of his spices, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the good ointment, and all the house of his vessels, and all that has been found in his treasures; there has not been a thing in his house, and in all his dominion, that Hezekiah has not showed them.
39.3: And Isaiah the prophet comes in to king Hezekiah, and says to him, `What said these men? and from where come they to you?' And Hezekiah says, `From a land afar off they have come to me--from Babylon.'
39.4: And he says, `What saw they in your house?' and Hezekiah says, `All that is in my house they saw; there has not been a thing that I have not showed them among my treasures.'
39.5: And Isaiah says to Hezekiah, `Hear a word of Jehovah of Hosts:
39.6: Indeed, days are coming, and borne has been all that is in your house, and that your fathers have treasured up till this day, to Babylon; there is not left a thing, said Jehovah;
39.7: and of your sons who come forth from you, whom you beget, they take, and they have been eunuchs in a palace of the king of Babylon.'
39.8: And Hezekiah says to Isaiah, `Good is the word of Jehovah that you have spoken;' and he says, `Because there is peace and truth in my days.'

40.1: Comfort you, comfort you, My people, says your God.
40.2: Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her, That her warfare has been completed, That accepted has been her punishment, That she has received from the hand of Jehovah Double for all her sins.
40.3: A voice is crying--in a wilderness--Prepare you the way of Jehovah, Make straight in a desert a highway to our God.
40.4: Every valley is raised up, And every mountain and hill become low, And the crooked place has become a plain, And the entangled places a valley.
40.5: And revealed has been the honour of Jehovah, And seen it have all flesh together, For the mouth of Jehovah has spoken.
40.6: A voice is saying, `Call,' And he said, `What do I call?' All flesh is grass, and all its goodliness is As a flower of the field:
40.7: Withered has grass, faded the flower, For the Spirit of Jehovah blew upon it, Surely the people is grass;
40.8: Withered has grass, faded the flower, But a word of our God rises for ever.
40.9: On a high mountain get you up, O Zion, Proclaiming tidings, Lift up with power your voice, O Jerusalem, proclaiming tidings, Lift up, fear not, say to cities of Judah, `Indeed, your God.'
40.10: Indeed, the Lord Jehovah with strength comes, And His arm is ruling for Him, Indeed, His hire is with Him, and His wage before Him.
40.11: As a shepherd His flock He feeds, With His arm He gathers lambs, And in His bosom He carries them: Suckling ones He leads.
40.12: Who has measured in the hollow of his hand the waters? And the heavens by a span has meted out, And comprehended in a measure the dust of the earth, And has weighed in scales the mountains, And the hills in a balance?
40.13: Who has meted out the Spirit of Jehovah, And, being His counsellor, does teach Him!
40.14: With whom consulted He, That he causes Him to understand? And teaches Him in the path of judgment, And teaches Him knowledge? And the way of understanding causes Him to know?
40.15: Indeed, nations as a drop from a bucket, And as small dust of the balance, have been reckoned, Indeed, isles as a small thing He takes up.
40.16: And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, Nor its beasts sufficient for a burnt-offering.
40.17: All the nations are as nothing before Him, Less than nothing and emptiness, They have been reckoned to Him.
40.18: And to whom do you liken God, And what likeness do you compare to Him?
40.19: The graven image poured out has a artisan, And a refiner with gold spreads it over, And chains of silver he is refining.
40.20: He who is poor by heave-offerings, A tree not rotten does choose, A skilful artisan he seeks for it, To establish a graven image--not moved.
40.21: Do you not know--do you not hear? Has it not been declared from the first to you? Have you not understood From the foundations of the earth?
40.22: He who is sitting on the circle of the earth, And its inhabitants are as grasshoppers, He who is stretching out as a thin thing the heavens, And spreads them as a tent to dwell in.
40.23: He who is making princes become nothing, Judges of earth as emptiness has made;
40.24: Yes, they have not been planted, Yes, they have not been sown, Yes, not taking root in the earth is their stock, And also He has blown upon them, and they wither, And a whirlwind as stubble takes them away.
40.25: And to whom do you liken Me, And am I equal? says the Holy One.
40.26: Lift up on high your eyes, And see--who has prepared these? He who is bringing out by number their host, To all of them by name He calls, By abundance of strength (And he is strong in power) not one is lacking.
40.27: Why do you say, O Jacob? and do you speak, O Israel? `My way has been hid from Jehovah, And from my God my judgment passes over.'
40.28: Have you not known? have you not heard? The God of the age--Jehovah, Preparer of the ends of the earth, Is not wearied nor fatigued, There is no searching of His understanding.
40.29: He is giving power to the weary, And to those not strong He increases might.
40.30: Even youths are wearied and fatigued, And young men utterly stumble,
40.31: But those expecting Jehovah pass to power, They raise up the pinion as eagles, They run and are not fatigued, They go on and do not faint!

41.1: Keep silent toward Me, O isles, And the peoples pass on to power, They come nigh, then they speak, `Together--to judgment we draw near.'
41.2: Who stirred up from the east a righteous one? He calls him to His foot, He gives before him nations, And kings He causes him to rule, He gives them as dust to his sword, As driven stubble to his bow.
41.3: He pursues them, he passes over in safety A path with his feet he enters not.
41.4: Who has worked and done, Calling the generations from the first? I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last I am He.
41.5: Seen have isles and fear, ends of the earth tremble, They have drawn near, yes, they come.
41.6: Each his neighbour they help, And to his brother he says, `Be strong.'
41.7: And strengthen does an artisan the refiner, A smoother with a hammer, Him who is beating on an anvil, Saying, `For joining it is good,' And he strengthens it with nails, it is not moved!
41.8: --And you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, Seed of Abraham, My lover,
41.9: Whom I have taken hold of, from the ends of the earth, And from its near places I have called you, And I say to you, My servant You are, I have chosen you, and not rejected you.
41.10: Be not afraid, for with you I am, Look not around, for I am your God, I have strengthened you, Yes, I have helped you, yes, I upheld you, With the right hand of My righteousness.
41.11: Indeed, all those displeased with you, They are ashamed and blush, They are as nothing, yes, perish Do the men who strive with you.
41.12: You seek them, and find them not, The men who debate with you, They are as nothing, yes, as nothing, The men who war with you.
41.13: For I, Jehovah your God, Am strengthening your right hand, He who is saying to you, `Fear not, I have helped you.'
41.14: Fear not, O worm Jacob, you men of Israel, I helped you, an affirmation of Jehovah, Even your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
41.15: Indeed, I have set you for a new sharp threshing instrument, Possessing teeth, you thresh mountains, And beat small, and hills as chaff you make.
41.16: You winnow them, and a wind lifts them up, And a whirlwind scatters them, And you--you rejoice in Jehovah, In the Holy One of Israel do boast yourself.
41.17: The poor and the needy are seeking water, And there is none, Their tongue with thirst has failed, I, Jehovah do answer them, The God of Israel--I forsake them not.
41.18: I open on high places rivers, And in midst of valleys fountains, I make a wilderness become a pond of water, And a dry land become springs of water.
41.19: I give in a wilderness the cedar, Shittah, and myrtle, and oil-tree, I set in a desert the fir-pine and box-wood together.
41.20: So that they see, and know, And regard, and act wisely together, For the hand of Jehovah has done this, And the Holy One of Israel has prepared it.
41.21: Bring near your cause, says Jehovah, Bring nigh your mighty ones, says the king of Jacob.
41.22: They bring nigh, and declare to us that which does happen, The first things--what they are declare you, And we set our heart, and know their latter end, Or the coming things cause us to hear.
41.23: Declare the things that are coming hereafter, And we know that you are gods, Yes, you may do good or do evil, And we look around and see it together.
41.24: Indeed, you are of nothing, and your work of nought, An abomination--it fixes on you.
41.25: I have stirred up one from the north, And he comes, From the rising of the sun he calls in My name, And he comes in on prefects as on clay, And as a potter treads down mire.
41.26: Who has declared from the first, and we know? And beforetime, and we say, `Righteous?' yes, there is none declaring, Yes, there is none proclaiming, Yes, there is none hearing your sayings.
41.27: First to Zion, Behold, behold them, And to Jerusalem one proclaiming tidings I give,
41.28: And I see that there is no man, Yes, of these that there is no counsellor, And I ask them, and they return word:
41.29: `Indeed, all of them are vanity, Nought are their works, Wind and emptiness their molten images!'

42.1: Indeed, My servant, I take hold on him, My chosen one--My soul has accepted, I have put My Spirit upon him, Judgment to nations he brings forth.
42.2: He does not cry, nor lift up, Nor cause his voice to be heard, in the street.
42.3: A bruised reed he breaks not, And dim flax he quenches not, To truth he brings forth judgment.
42.4: He does not become weak nor bruised, Till he sets judgment in the earth, And for his law isles wait with hope.
42.5: Thus said God, Jehovah, preparing The heavens, and stretching them out, Spreading out the earth and its productions, Giving breath to the people on it, And spirit to those walking in it.
42.6: I, Jehovah, did call you in righteousness, And I lay hold on your hand, and keep you, And I give you for a covenant of a people, And a light of nations.
42.7: To open the eyes of the blind, To bring forth from prison the bound one, From the house of restraint those sitting in darkness.
42.8: I am Jehovah, this is My name, And My honour to another I give not, Nor My praise to graven images.
42.9: The former things, indeed, have come, And new things I am declaring, Before they spring up I cause you to hear.
42.10: Sing to Jehovah a new song, His praise from the end of the earth, You who are going down to the sea, and its fulness, Isles, and their inhabitants.
42.11: The wilderness and its cities do lift up the voice, The villages Kedar does inhabit, Sing do the inhabitants of Sela, From the top of mountains they cry.
42.12: They ascribe to Jehovah honour, And His praise in the isles they declare.
42.13: Jehovah as a mighty one goes forth. As a man of war He stirs up zeal, He cries, yes, He shrieks, Against His enemies He shows Himself mighty.
42.14: I have kept silent from of old, I keep silent, I refrain myself, As a travailing woman I cry out, I desolate and swallow up together.
42.15: I make waste mountains and hills, And all their herbs I dry up, And I have made rivers become isles, And ponds I dry up.
42.16: And I have caused the blind to go, In a way they have not known, In paths they have not known I cause them to tread, I make a dark place before them become light, And unlevelled places become a plain, These are the things I have done to them, And I have not forsaken them.
42.17: Removed backward--utterly ashamed, Are those trusting in a graven image, Those saying to a molten image, `You are our gods.'
42.18: You deaf, hear; and you blind, look to see.
42.19: Who is blind but My servant? And deaf as My messenger I send? Who is blind as he who is at peace, Yes, blind, as the servant of Jehovah?
42.20: Seeing many things, and you observe not, Opening ears, and he hears not.
42.21: Jehovah has delight for the sake of His righteousness, He magnifies law, and makes honourable.
42.22: And this is a people seized and spoiled, Snared in holes--all of them, And in houses of restraint they were hidden, They have been for a prey, And there is no deliverer, A spoil, and none is saying, `Restore.'
42.23: Who among you gives ear to this? Attends, and hears afterwards.
42.24: Who has given Jacob for a spoil, And Israel to the spoilers? Is it not Jehovah--He against whom we sinned? Yes, they have not been willing in His ways to walk, Nor have they hearkened to His law.
42.25: And He pours on him fury, His anger, and the strength of battle, And it sets him on fire round about, And he has not known, And it burns against him, and he lays it not to heart!

43.1: And now, thus said Jehovah, Your Creator, O Jacob, and your Fashioner, O Israel, Be not afraid, for I have redeemed you, I have called on your name--you are Mine.
43.2: When you pass into waters, I am with you, And into floods, they do not overflow you, When you go into fire, you are not burnt, And a flame does not burn against you.
43.3: For I--Jehovah your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Saviour, I have appointed Egypt your atonement, Cush and Seba in your stead.
43.4: Since you were precious in My eyes, You were honoured, and I have loved you, And I appoint men in your stead, And peoples instead of your life.
43.5: Be not afraid, for I am with you, From the east I bring in your seed, And from the west I gather you.
43.6: I am saying to the north, `Give up,' And to the south, `Restrain not.' Bring in My sons from afar, And My daughters from the end of the earth.
43.7: Every one who is called by My name, Even for My honour I have created him, I have formed him, yes, I have made him.
43.8: He brought out a blind people who have eyes, And deaf ones who have ears.
43.9: All the nations have been gathered together, And the peoples are assembled, Who among them declares this, And former things causes us to hear? They give their witnesses, And they are declared righteous, And they hear and say, `Truth.'
43.10: You are My witnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And My servant whom I have chosen, So that you know and give credence to Me, And understand that I am He, Before Me there was no God formed, And after Me there is none.
43.11: I--I am Jehovah, And besides Me there is no saviour.
43.12: I--I declared, and saved, and proclaimed, And there is no stranger with you, And you are My witnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And I am God.
43.13: Even from the day I am He, And there is no deliverer from My hand, I work, and who does turn it back?
43.14: Thus said Jehovah, your Redeemer, The Holy One of Israel: `For your sake I have sent to Babylon, And caused bars to descend--all of them, And the Chaldeans, whose song is in the ships.
43.15: I am Jehovah, your Holy One, Creator of Israel, your King.'
43.16: Thus said Jehovah, Who is giving in the sea a way, And in the strong waters a path.
43.17: Who is bringing forth chariot and horse, A force, even a strong one: `Together they lie down--they rise not, They have been extinguished, As flax they have been quenched.'
43.18: Remember not former things, And ancient things consider not.
43.19: Indeed, I am doing a new thing, now it springs up, Do you not know it? Yes, I put in a wilderness a way, In a desolate place--floods.
43.20: Honour me does the beast of the field, Dragons and daughters of an ostrich, For I have given in a wilderness waters, Floods in a desolate place, To give drink to My people--My chosen.
43.21: This people I have formed for Myself, My praise they recount.
43.22: And Me you have not called, O Jacob, For you have been wearied of me, O Israel,
43.23: You have not brought in to Me, The lamb of your burnt-offerings, And with your sacrifices you have not honoured Me, I have not caused you to serve with a present, Nor wearied you with frankincense.
43.24: You have not bought for Me with money sweet cane, And with the fat of your sacrifices have not filled Me, Only--you have caused Me to serve with your sins, You have wearied Me with your iniquities.
43.25: I--I am He who is blotting out Your transgressions for My own sake, And your sins I do not remember.
43.26: Cause me to remember--we are judged together, Declare you that you may be justified.
43.27: Your first father sinned, And your interpreters transgressed against me,
43.28: And I pollute princes of the sanctuary, And I give Jacob to destruction, and Israel to revilings!

44.1: And now, hear, O Jacob, My servant, And Israel, whom I have fixed on:
44.2: Thus said Jehovah, your Maker, and your Former, From the womb He does help you; Fear not, my servant Jacob, And Jeshurun, whom I have fixed on.
44.3: For I pour waters on a thirsty one, And floods on a dry land, I pour My Spirit on your seed, And My blessing on your offspring.
44.4: And they have sprung up as among grass, As willows by streams of water.
44.5: This one says, For Jehovah I am, And this calls himself by the name of Jacob, And this one writes with his hand, `For Jehovah,' and by the name of Israel surnames himself.
44.6: Thus said Jehovah, king of Israel, And his Redeemer, Jehovah of Hosts: `I am the first, and I the last, And besides Me there is no God.
44.7: And who as I, does call and declare it, And arrange it for Me, Since My placing the people of antiquity, And things that are coming, And those that do come, declare they to them?
44.8: Fear not, nor be afraid, Have I not from that time caused you to hear, and declared? And you are My witnesses, Is there a God besides Me? yes, there is none, A Rock I have not known.
44.9: Framers of a graven image are all of them emptiness, And their desirable things do not profit, And their own witnesses they are, They see not, nor know, that they may be ashamed.
44.10: Who has formed a god, And a molten image poured out--not profitable?
44.11: Indeed, all his companions are ashamed, As to artisans--they are of men, All of them gather together, they stand up, They fear, they are ashamed together.
44.12: He has worked iron with an axe, And has worked with coals, And with hammers does form it, And does work it by his powerful arm, Yes, he is hungry, and there is no power, He does not drink water, and he is wearied.
44.13: He has worked with wood, He has stretched out a rule, He does mark it out with a line, He makes it with carving tools, And with a compass he marks it out, And makes it according to the form of a man, According to the beauty of a man, To remain in the house.
44.14: Cutting down to himself cedars, He takes also a cypress, and an oak, And he strengthens it for himself Among the trees of a forest, He has planted an ash, and the shower does nourish it.
44.15: And it has been for man to burn, And he takes of them, and becomes warm, Yes, he kindles it, and has baked bread, Yes, he makes a god, and bows himself, He has made it a graven image, And he falls down to it.
44.16: Half of it he has burnt in the fire, By this half of it he eats flesh, He roasts a roasting, and is satisfied, Yes, he is warm, and says: `Aha, I have become warm, I have enjoyed the light.
44.17: And its remnant for a god he has made--For his graven image, He falls down to it, and worships, And prays to it, and he says, `Deliver me, for my god you are.'
44.18: They have not known, nor do they understand, For He has daubed their eyes from seeing, Their heart from acting wisely.
44.19: And none does turn it back to his heart, Nor has knowledge nor understanding to say, `Half of it I have burned in the fire, Yes, also, I have baked bread over its coals, I roast flesh and I eat, And its remnant for an abomination I make, To the stock of a tree I fall down.'
44.20: Feeding on ashes, the heart is deceived, It has turned him aside, And he delivers not his soul, nor says: `Is there not a lie in my right hand?'
44.21: Remember these, O Jacob, and Israel, For My servant you are, I formed you, a servant to Me you are, O Israel, you do not forget Me.
44.22: I have blotted out, as by a thick cloud, Your transgressions, And as by a cloud your sins, Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.
44.23: Sing, O heavens, for Jehovah has worked, Shout, O lower parts of earth, Break forth, O mountains, with singing, Forest, and every tree in it, For Jehovah has redeemed Jacob, And in Israel He does beautify Himself.
44.24: Thus said Jehovah, your redeemer, And your framer from the womb: `I am Jehovah, doing all things, Stretching out the heavens by Myself, Spreading out the earth--who is with Me?
44.25: Making void the tokens of devisers, And diviners it makes mad, Turning the wise backward, And their knowledge it makes foolish.
44.26: Confirming the word of His servant, The counsel of His messengers it perfects, Who is saying of Jerusalem, She is inhabited, And of cities of Judah, They shall be built, and her wastes I raise up,
44.27: Who is saying to the deep, Be dry, and your rivers I cause to dry up,
44.28: Who is saying of Cyrus, My shepherd, And all my delight He does perfect, So as to say of Jerusalem, You are built, And of the temple, You are founded.

45.1: Thus said Jehovah, To His anointed, to Cyrus, Whose right hand I have laid hold on, To subdue nations before him, Yes, loins of kings I loose, To open before him two-leaved doors, Yes, gates are not shut:
45.2: `I go before you, and crooked places make straight, Two-leaved doors of brass I shiver, And bars of iron I cut asunder,
45.3: And have given to you treasures of darkness, Even treasures of secret places, So that you know that I, Jehovah, Who am calling on your name-- am the God of Israel.
45.4: For the sake of my servant Jacob, And of Israel My chosen, I call also you by your name, I surname you, And you have not known Me.
45.5: I am Jehovah, and there is none else, Except Me there is no God, I gird you, and you have not known Me.
45.6: So that they know from the rising of the sun, And from the west, that there is none besides Me, I am Jehovah, and there is none else,
45.7: Forming light, and preparing darkness, Making peace, and preparing evil, I am Jehovah, doing all these things.'
45.8: Drop, you heavens, from above, And clouds do cause righteousness to flow, Earth opens, and they are fruitful, Salvation and righteousness spring up together, I, Jehovah, have prepared it.
45.9: Woe to him who is striving with his Former, (A potsherd with potsherds of the ground!) Does clay say to its Framer, `What do you?' And your work, `He has no hands?'
45.10: Woe to him who is saying to a father, `What do you beget?' Or to a wife, `What do you bring forth?
45.11: Thus said Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, and his Former: Ask Me of the things coming concerning My sons, Yes, concerning the work of My hands, you command Me.'
45.12: I made earth, and man on it prepared, I--My hands stretched out the heavens, And all their host I have commanded.
45.13: I have stirred him up in righteousness, And all his ways I make straight, He does build My city, and My captivity does send out, Not for price, nor for bribe, said Jehovah of Hosts.
45.14: Thus said Jehovah, `The labour of Egypt, And the merchandise of Cush, And of the Sebaim--men of measure, To you pass over, and your they are, After you they go, in fetters they pass over, And to you they bow themselves, To you they pray: Only in you is God, And there is none else, no other God.
45.15: Surely You are a God hiding Yourself, God of Israel--Saviour!
45.16: They have been ashamed, And they have even blushed--all of them, Together gone in confusion have those carving images.
45.17: Israel has been saved in Jehovah, A salvation age-during! You are not ashamed nor confounded To the ages of eternity!
45.18: For thus said Jehovah, Creator of heaven, He is God, Former of earth, and its Maker, He established it--not empty He prepared it, For inhabiting He formed it: `I am Jehovah, and there is none else.
45.19: Not in secret have I spoken, in a dark place of the earth, I have not said to the seed of Jacob, In vain seek you Me, I am Jehovah, speaking righteousness, Declaring uprightness.
45.20: Be gathered, and come in, Come nigh together, you escaped of the nations, They have not known, Who are lifting up the wood of their graven image, And praying to a god that saves not.
45.21: Declare you, and bring near, Yes, they take counsel together, Who has proclaimed this from of old? From that time has declared it? Is it not I--Jehovah? And there is no other god besides Me, A God righteous and saving, there is none save Me.
45.22: Turn to Me, and be saved, all ends of the earth, For I am God, and there is none else.
45.23: By Myself I have sworn, Gone out from my mouth in righteousness has a word, And it turns not back, That to Me, bow does every knee, every tongue swear.
45.24: Only in Jehovah, said has one, Have I righteousness and strength, To Him he comes in, And ashamed are all those displeased with Him.
45.25: In Jehovah are all the seed of Israel justified, And they boast themselves.'

46.1: Bowed down has Bel, stooping is Nebo, Their idols have been for the beast and for cattle, Your burdens are loaded, a burden to the weary.
46.2: They have stooped, they have bowed together, They have not been able to deliver the burden, And themselves into captivity have gone.
46.3: Hearken to Me, O house of Jacob, And all the remnant of Israel, Who are borne from the belly, Who are carried from the womb,
46.4: Even to old age I am He, and to grey hairs I carry, I made, and I bear, yes, I carry and deliver.
46.5: To whom do you liken Me, and make equal? And compare Me, that we may be like?
46.6: --They are pouring out gold from a bag, And silver on the beam they weigh, They hire a refiner, and he makes it a god, They fall down, yes, they bow themselves.
46.7: They lift him up on the shoulder, They carry him, and cause him to rest in his place, And he stands, from his place he moves not, Yes, one cries to him, and he answers not, From his adversity he saves him not.
46.8: Remember this, and show yourselves men, Turn it back, O transgressors, to the heart.
46.9: Remember former things of old, For I am Mighty, and there is none else, God--and there is none like Me.
46.10: Declaring from the beginning the latter end, And from of old that which has not been done, Saying, `My counsel does stand, And all My delight I do.'
46.11: Calling from the east a ravenous bird, From a far land the man of My counsel, Yes, I have spoken, yes, I bring it in, I have formed it, yes, I do it.
46.12: Hearken to Me, you mighty in heart, Who are far from righteousness.
46.13: I have brought near My righteousness, It is not far off, And My salvation--it does not tarry, And I have given in Zion salvation, To Israel My glory!

47.1: Come down, and sit on the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, Sit on the earth, there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to you, `O tender and delicate one.'
47.2: Take millstones, and grind flour, Remove your veil, draw up the skirt, Uncover the leg, pass over the floods.
47.3: Revealed is your nakedness, yes, seen is your reproach, Vengeance I take, and I meet not a man.
47.4: Our redeemer is Jehovah of Hosts, His name is the Holy One of Israel.
47.5: Sit silent, and go into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to you, `Mistress of kingdoms.'
47.6: I have been wroth against My people, I have polluted My inheritance And I give them into your hand, You have not appointed for them mercies, On the aged you have made your yoke very heavy,
47.7: And you say, `To the age I am mistress,' While you have not laid these things to your heart, You have not remembered the latter end of it.
47.8: And now, hear this, O luxurious one, Who is sitting confidently--Who is saying in her heart, `I am, and none else, I sit not a widow, nor know bereavement.'
47.9: And come in to you do these two things, In a moment, in one day, childlessness and widowhood, According to their perfection they have come upon you, In the multitude of your sorceries, In the exceeding might of your charms.
47.10: And you are confident in your wickedness, You have said, `There is none seeing me,' Your wisdom and your knowledge, It is turning you back, And you say in your heart, `I am, and none else.'
47.11: And come in on you has evil, You know not its rising, And fall on you does mischief, You are not able to pacify it, And come on you suddenly does desolation, You know not.
47.12: Stand, I pray you, in your charms, And in the multitude of your sorceries, In which you have laboured from your youth, It may be you are able to profit, It may be you do terrify!
47.13: You have been wearied in the multitude of your counsels, Stand up, I pray you, and save you, Let the charmers of the heavens, Those looking on the stars, Those teaching concerning the months, From those things that come on you!
47.14: Indeed, they have been as stubble! Fire has burned them, They deliver not themselves from the power of the flame, There is not a coal to warm them, a light to sit before it.
47.15: So have they been to you with whom you have laboured, Your merchants from your youth, Each to his passage they have wandered, Your saviour is not!

48.1: Hear you this, O house of Jacob, Who are called by the name of Israel, And from the waters of Judah came out, Who are swearing by the name of Jehovah, And of the God of Israel make mention, Not in truth nor in righteousness.
48.2: For from the Holy City they have been called, And on the God of Israel been supported, Jehovah of Hosts is His name.
48.3: The former things from that time I declared, And from my mouth they have gone forth, And I proclaim them, Suddenly I have done, and it comes.
48.4: From my knowing that you are obstinate, And a sinew of iron your neck, And your forehead brass,
48.5: And I declare to you from that time, Before it comes I have caused you to hear, Lest you say, `My idol has done them, And my graven image, And my molten image did command them.
48.6: You have heard, see the whole of it, And you, do you not declare? I have caused you to hear new things from this time, And things reserved that you knew not.
48.7: Now they have been produced and not from that time, Yes, before the day, and you have not heard them, Lest you say, `Indeed, I have known them.'
48.8: Yes, you have not heard, Yes, you have not known, Yes, from that time not opened has your ear, For I have known you deal treacherously, And `Transgressor from the belly,' One is crying to you.
48.9: For My name's sake I defer My anger, And My praise I restrain for you, So as not to cut you off.
48.10: Indeed, I have refined you, and not with silver, I have chosen you in a furnace of affliction.
48.11: For My sake, for My own sake, I do it, For how is it polluted? And My honour to another I give not.
48.12: Hearken to me, O Jacob, and Israel, My called one, I am He, I am first, and I am last;
48.13: Also, My hand has founded earth, And My right hand stretched out the heavens, I am calling to them, they stand together.
48.14: Be gathered all of you, and hear, Who among them did declare these things? Jehovah has loved him, He does His pleasure on Babylon, And His arm is on the Chaldeans.
48.15: I--I have spoken, yes, I have called him, I have brought him in, And he has made prosperous his way.
48.16: Come you near to me, hear this, Not from the beginning in secret spoke I, From the time of its being, there am I, And now the Lord Jehovah has sent me, and His Spirit.
48.17: Thus said Jehovah, your redeemer, The Holy One of Israel, `I am Jehovah your God, teaching you to profit, Causing you to tread in the way you go.
48.18: O that you had attended to My commands, Then as a river is your peace, And your righteousness as billows of the sea,
48.19: And as sand is your seed, And the offspring of your bowels as its gravel, Not cut off nor destroyed his name before Me.
48.20: Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, With a voice of singing declare, Cause you this to be heard, Bring it forth to the end of the earth, Say, Redeemed has Jehovah His servant Jacob.
48.21: And they have not thirsted in waste places, He has caused them to go on, Waters from a rock he has caused to flow to them, Yes, he cleaves a rock, and flow do waters.
48.22: There is no peace, said Jehovah, to the wicked!

49.1: Hearken, O isles, to me, And attend, O peoples, from afar, Jehovah from the womb has called me, From the bowels of my mother He has made mention of my name.
49.2: And he makes my mouth as a sharp sword, In the shadow of His hand He has hid me, And He makes me for a clear arrow, In His quiver He has hid me.
49.3: And He says to me, `My servant You are, O Israel, In whom I beautify Myself.'
49.4: And I said, `For a vain thing I laboured, For emptiness and vanity my power I consumed, But my judgment is with Jehovah, And my wage with my God.
49.5: And now, said Jehovah, who is forming me from the belly for a servant to Him, To bring back Jacob to Him, (Though Israel is not gathered, Yet I am honoured in the eyes of Jehovah, And my God has been my strength.)
49.6: And He says, `It has been a light thing That you are to Me for a servant To raise up the tribes of Jacob, And the preserved of Israel to bring back, And I have given you for a light of nations, To be My salvation to the end of the earth.'
49.7: Thus said Jehovah, Redeemer of Israel, His Holy One, To the despised in soul, To the abominated of a nation, To the servant of rulers: `Kings see, and have risen, princes, and worship, For the sake of Jehovah, who is faithful, The Holy of Israel, and He chooses you.'
49.8: Thus said Jehovah: `In a time of good pleasure I answered you, And in a day of salvation I helped you, And I keep you, and give you, For a covenant of the people, To establish the earth, To cause to inherit desolate inheritances.
49.9: To say to the bound, Go out, To those in darkness, Be uncovered. On the ways they feed, And in all high places is their pasture.
49.10: They do not hunger, nor thirst, Nor smite them does mirage and sun, For He who is pitying them does lead them, And by fountains of waters does tend them.
49.11: And I have made all My mountains for a way, And My highways are lifted up.
49.12: Indeed, these from afar come in, And indeed, these from the north, and from the sea, And these from the land of Sinim.
49.13: Sing, O heavens, and joy, O earth, And break forth, O mountains, with singing, For comforted has Jehovah His people, And His afflicted ones He does pity.
49.14: And Zion says, `Jehovah has forsaken me, And my Lord has forgotten me.'
49.15: Forget does a woman her suckling, The loved one--the son of her womb? Yes, these forget--but I--I forget not you.
49.16: Indeed, on the palms of the hand I have graven you, Your walls are before Me continually.
49.17: Hastened have those building you, Those destroying you, and laying you waste, go out from you.
49.18: Lift up round about your eyes and see, All of them have been gathered, They have come to you. I live, an affirmation of Jehovah! Surely all of them as an ornament you put on, And you bind them on like a bride.
49.19: Because your wastes, and your desolate places, And the land of your ruins, Surely now are straitened because of inhabitants, And far off have been those consuming you.
49.20: Again do the sons of your bereavement say in your ears: `The place is too strait for me, Come nigh to me--and I dwell.'
49.21: And you have said in your heart: `Who has begotten for me--these? And I bereaved and gloomy, A captive, and turned aside, And these--who has nourished? Indeed, I--I was left by myself, these--from where are they?
49.22: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: `Indeed, I lift up to nations My hand, And to peoples I raise up My ensign, And they have brought your sons in the bosom, And your daughters on the shoulder are carried.
49.23: And kings have been your nursing fathers, And their princesses your nursing mothers; Face to the earth--they bow down to you, And the dust of your feet they lick up, And you have known that I am Jehovah, That those expecting Me are not ashamed.
49.24: Is prey taken from the mighty? And the captive of the righteous delivered?
49.25: For thus said Jehovah: Even the captive of the mighty is taken, And the prey of the terrible is delivered, And with your striver I strive, and your sons I save.
49.26: And I have caused your oppressors to eat their own flesh, And as new wine they drink their own blood, And known have all flesh that I, Jehovah, Your saviour, and your redeemer, Am the Mighty One of Jacob!'

50.1: Thus said Jehovah: `Where is this--the bill of your mother's divorce, Whom I sent away? Or to which of My creditors have I sold you? Indeed, for your iniquities you have been sold, And for your transgressions Has your mother been sent away.
50.2: Wherefore have I come, and there is no one? I called, and there is none answering, Has My hand been at all short of redemption? And is there not in me power to deliver? Indeed, by My rebuke I dry up a sea, I make rivers a wilderness, Their fish stinks, for there is no water, And dies with thirst.
50.3: I clothe the heavens with blackness, And sackcloth I make their covering.
50.4: The Lord Jehovah has given to me The tongue of taught ones, To know to aid the weary by a word, He wakes morning by morning, He wakes for me an ear to hear as taught ones.
50.5: The Lord Jehovah opened for me the ear, And I rebelled not--backward I moved not.
50.6: My back I have given to those smiting, And my cheeks to those plucking out, My face I hid not from shame and spitting.
50.7: And the Lord Jehovah gives help to me, Therefore I have not been ashamed, Therefore I have set my face as a flint, And I know that I am not ashamed.
50.8: Near is He who is justifying me, Who does contend with me? We stand together, who is my opponent? Let him come nigh to me.
50.9: Indeed, the Lord Jehovah gives help to me, Who is he that declares me wicked? Indeed, all of them as a garment wear out, A moth does eat them.
50.10: Who is among you, fearing Jehovah, Hearkening to the voice of His servant, That has walked in dark places, And there is no brightness for him? Let him trust in the name of Jehovah, And lean upon his God.
50.11: Indeed, all you kindling a fire, girding on sparks, Walk you in the light of your fire, And in the sparks you have caused to burn, From my hand has this been to you, In grief you lie down!

51.1: Hearken to Me, you pursuing righteousness, Seeking Jehovah, Look attentively to the rock--you have been hewn, And to the hole of the pit--you have been digged.
51.2: Look attentively to Abraham your father, And to Sarah--she brings you forth, For--one--I have called him, And I bless him, and multiply him.
51.3: For Jehovah has comforted Zion, He has comforted all her wastes, And He sets her wilderness as Eden, And her desert as a garden of Jehovah, Joy, yes, gladness is found in her, Confession, and the voice of song.
51.4: Attend to Me, O My people, And, O My nation, to Me give ear. For a law from Me goes out, And My judgment to the light, Peoples I do cause to rest.
51.5: Near is My righteousness, Gone out has My salvation and My arms, Peoples they judge, on Me isles do wait, Yes, on My arm they do wait with hope.
51.6: Lift you up to the heavens your eyes, And look attentively to the earth beneath, For the heavens as smoke have vanished, And the earth as a garment wearies out, And its inhabitants as gnats do die, And My salvation is to the age, And My righteousness is not broken.
51.7: Hearken to Me, you who know righteousness, A people, in whose heart is My law, Fear you not the reproach of men, And for their reviling be not affrighted,
51.8: For as a garment eat them does a moth, And as wool eat them does a worm, And My righteousness is to the age, And My salvation to all generations.
51.9: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of Jehovah, Awake, as in days of old, generations of the ages, Are not You it that is hewing down Rahab, Piercing a dragon!
51.10: Are not You it that is drying up a sea, Waters of a great deep? That has made deep places of a sea A way for the passing of the redeemed?
51.11: And the ransomed of Jehovah turn back, And they have come to Zion with singing, And joy age-during is on their head, Gladness and joy they attain, Fled away have sorrow and sighing,
51.12: I--I am He--your comforter, Who are you--and you are afraid of man? he dies! And of the son of man--grass he is made!
51.13: And you do forget Jehovah your maker, Who is stretching out the heavens, and founding earth, And you do fear continually all the day, Because of the fury of the oppressor, As he has prepared to destroy. And where is the fury of the oppressor?
51.14: Hastened has a wanderer to be loosed, And he does not die at the pit, And his bread is not lacking.
51.15: And I am Jehovah your God, Quieting the sea, when its billows roar, Jehovah of Hosts is His name.
51.16: And I put My words in your mouth, And with the shadow of My hand have covered you, To plant the heavens, and to found earth, And to say to Zion, `My people are you.'
51.17: Stir yourself, stir yourself, rise, Jerusalem, Who have drunk from the hand of Jehovah The cup of His fury, The goblet, the cup of trembling, you have drunk, You have wrung out.
51.18: There is not a leader to her Out of all the sons she has borne, And there is none laying hold on her hand Out of all the sons she has nourished.
51.19: These two are meeting you, who is moved for you? Spoiling and destruction--Famine and sword, who--I comfort you?
51.20: Your sons have been wrapped up, they have lain down, At the head of all out places, as a wild ox in a net, They are full of the fury of Jehovah, The rebuke of Your God.
51.21: Therefore, hear, I pray you, this, O afflicted and drunken one, and not with wine,
51.22: Thus said your Lord Jehovah, and your God, He pleads for his people: `Indeed, I have taken out of your hand the cup of trembling, The goblet, the cup of My fury, You do not add to drink it any more.
51.23: And I have put it into the hand of those afflicting you, Who have said to your soul, Bow down, and we pass over, And you make as the earth your body, And as the street to those passing by!'

52.1: Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion, Put on the garments of your beauty, Jerusalem--the Holy City; For enter no more into you again, Do the uncircumcised and unclean.
52.2: Shake yourself from dust, arise, sit, O Jerusalem, Bands of your neck have loosed themselves, O captive, daughter of Zion.
52.3: For thus said Jehovah: `For nought you have been sold, And not by money are you redeemed.'
52.4: For thus said the Lord Jehovah: `To Egypt My people went down at first to sojourn there, And Asshur--for nought he has oppressed it.
52.5: And now, what--to Me here, An affirmation of Jehovah, That taken is My people for nought? Its rulers cause howling, --an affirmation of Jehovah, And continually all the day My name is despised.
52.6: Therefore does My people know My name, Therefore, in that day, Surely I am He who is speaking, behold Me.'
52.7: How comely on the mountains, Have been the feet of one proclaiming tidings, Sounding peace, proclaiming good tidings, Sounding salvation, Saying to Zion, `Reigned has your God.'
52.8: The voice of your watchmen! They have lifted up the voice, together they cry aloud, Because eye to eye they see, in Jehovah's turning back to Zion.
52.9: Break forth, sing together, O wastes of Jerusalem, For Jehovah has comforted His people, He has redeemed Jerusalem.
52.10: Jehovah has made bare His holy arm Before the eyes of all the nations, And seen have all the ends of the earth, The salvation of our God.
52.11: Turn aside, turn aside, go out from there, The unclean touch not, go out from her midst, Be you pure, who are bearing the weapons of Jehovah.
52.12: For not in haste do you go out, Yes, with flight you go not on, For going before you is Jehovah, And gathering you is the God of Israel!
52.13: Indeed, My servant does act wisely, He is high, and has been lifted up, And has been very high.
52.14: As astonished at you have been many, (So marred by man his appearance, And his form by sons of men.)
52.15: So does he sprinkle many nations. Concerning him kings shut their mouth, For that which was not recounted to them they have seen, And that which they had not heard they have understood!

53.1: Who has given credence to that which we heard? And the arm of Jehovah, On whom has it been revealed?
53.2: Yes, he comes up as a tender plant before Him, And as a root out of a dry land, He has no form, nor honour, when we observe him, Nor appearance, when we desire him.
53.3: He is despised, and left of men, A man of pains, and acquainted with sickness, And as one hiding the face from us, He is despised, and we esteemed him not.
53.4: Surely our sicknesses he has borne, And our pains--he has carried them, And we--we have esteemed him plagued, Smitten of God, and afflicted.
53.5: And he is pierced for our transgressions, Bruised for our iniquities, The chastisement of our peace is on him, And by his bruise there is healing to us.
53.6: All of us like sheep have wandered, Each to his own way we have turned, And Jehovah has caused to meet on him, The punishment of us all.
53.7: It has been exacted, and he has answered, And he opens not his mouth, As a lamb to the slaughter he is brought, And as a sheep before its shearers is dumb, And he opens not his mouth.
53.8: By restraint and by judgment he has been taken, And of his generation who does meditate, That he has been cut off from the land of the living? By the transgression of My people he is plagued,
53.9: And it appoints with the wicked his grave, And with the rich are his high places, Because he has done no violence, Nor is deceit in his mouth.
53.10: And Jehovah has delighted to bruise him, He has made him sick, If his soul does make an offering for guilt, He sees seed--he prolongs days, And the pleasure of Jehovah in his hand does prosper.
53.11: Of the labour of his soul he sees--he is satisfied, Through his knowledge give righteousness Does the righteous one, My servant, to many, And their iniquities he does bear.
53.12: Therefore I give a portion to him among the many, And with the mighty he apportions spoil, Because that he exposed to death his soul, And with transgressors he was numbered, And he the sin of many has borne, And for transgressors he intercedes.

54.1: Sing, O barren, she has not borne! Break forth with singing, and cry aloud, She has not brought forth! For more are the sons of the desolate, Than the sons of the married one, said Jehovah.
54.2: Enlarge the place of your tent, And the curtains of your tabernacles they stretch out, Restrain not--lengthen your cords, And your pins make strong.
54.3: For right and left you break forth, And your seed does nations possess,
54.4: And desolate cities they cause to be inhabited. Fear not, for you are not ashamed, Nor blush, for you are not confounded, For the shame of your youth you forget, And the reproach of your widowhood You do not remember any more.
54.5: For your Maker is your husband, Jehovah of Hosts is His name, And your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel, `God of all the earth,' He is called.
54.6: For, as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, Called you has Jehovah, Even a youthful wife when she is refused, said your God.
54.7: In a small moment I have forsaken you, And in great mercies I do gather you,
54.8: In overflowing wrath I hid my face for a moment from you, And in kindness age-during I have loved you, Said your Redeemer--Jehovah!
54.9: For, the waters of Noah is this to Me, In that I have sworn--the waters of Noah Do not pass again over the earth--So I have sworn, Wrath is not upon you, Nor rebuke against you.
54.10: For the mountains depart, and the hills remove, And My kindness from you departs not, And the covenant of My peace removes not, Said has your loving one--Jehovah.
54.11: O afflicted, storm-tossed, not comforted, Indeed, I am laying with cement your stones, And have founded you with sapphires,
54.12: And have made of agate your pinnacles, And your gates of carbuncle stones, And all your border of stones of delight,
54.13: And all your sons are taught of Jehovah, And abundant is the peace of your sons.
54.14: In righteousness you establish yourself, Be far from oppression, for you fear not, And from ruin, for it comes not near to you.
54.15: Indeed, he does diligently assemble without My desire, Who has assembled near you? By you he falls!
54.16: Indeed, I--I have prepared an artisan, Blowing on a fire of coals, And bringing out an instrument for his work, And I have prepared a destroyer to destroy.
54.17: No weapon formed against you prospers, And every tongue rising against you, In judgment you condemn. This is the inheritance of the servants of Jehovah, And their righteousness from me, an affirmation of Jehovah!

55.1: Ho, every thirsty one, come you to the waters, And he who has no money, Come you, buy and eat, yes, come, buy Without money and without price, wine and milk.
55.2: Why do you weigh money for that which is not bread? And your labour for that which is not for satiety? Hearken diligently to me, and eat good, And your soul does delight itself in fatness.
55.3: Incline your ear, and come to me, Hear, and your soul does live, And I make for you a covenant age-during, The kind acts of David--that are stedfast.
55.4: Indeed, a witness to peoples I have given him, A leader and commander to peoples.
55.5: Indeed, a nation you know not, you call, And a nation who know you not to you do run, For the sake of Jehovah your God, And for the Holy One of Israel, Because He has beautified you.
